## Addendum 278: Theorem 1aq landed — the arithmetic section: the half-shift lattice's distinguished status among Weil test-function cones; hostile round 175 next

**The commission.** The owner asked "check whether the half-shift
lattice w = d+½ has any distinguished status among Weil
test-function cones," reviewed the assessment, and commissioned
the landing ("land it").

**The content.** Under the critical-line coordinate w = s − ½ the
committed lattice is exactly the integer ladder s = d+1 — one
fact seen independently on all four sides of the explicit
formula, each an iff at the translate α = ½ among unit-spaced
decay lattices w = d + α: A1 the prime side is ζ-integer
evaluation (Σ Λ(n)n^(−(w+½)) = −ζ′/ζ(d+1), Euler terms
ln p/(p^(d+1)−1) with integer denominators — already silently
present in the bridge identity's s = d+1); A2 the pole term is
unit fractions (2w/(w²−¼) = 1/d + 1/(d+1) exactly; integer-w
values are consecutive-unit-fraction sums for no integer, an
odd/even reduced-denominator obstruction); A3 the kernel poles
sit at integer heights on the displaced curve
((γ+i/2)² + w² = (γ−id)(γ+i(d+1)); algebraically w²−¼ = d(d+1),
exact over the full committed range — the source of the (s, s−1)
telescoping and the 2s−1 = 2w normalization); A4 the
functional-equation involution s ↔ 1−s is the evenness w ↔ −w
exactly in the half-shift coordinate (R1's cosh((β−½)t)
symmetrization); A5 the archimedean argument ¼ + w/2 = (d+1)/2
lands on the ψ closed-form ladder. AND the counter-theorem: the
cone's positivity geometry is lattice-INDEPENDENT (R2's on-line
closed form, edge ratio, and strip-boundary sign reproduced
verbatim at the non-lattice pairs (1.7, 2.9) and (2.13, 5.41)) —
the half-shift buys no positivity advantage. The wall reframe:
the lattice is the maximal exactly-computable slice of the Weil
framework — why the arc's exact rationals (9/11, 1/297, 1/243,
the bridge's unit fractions) had to appear — and R4's wall is the
same fact from the other side: the rational section is where
positivity is classical bookkeeping; beyond its reach is RH.
Honest scope: category (a); the integralities are individually
classical background — the theorem is the identification and the
two-sidedness; consistency texture under Check 8, not forcing; no
RH leverage in either direction.

**The instrument.** `cascade_arithmetic_section.py`, 10 gates,
exit-gated, first clean run 10/0: g1 A2 exact rationals + the
integer-w counter-gate (m-scan); g2 A3 exact over d ∈ [1, 217] +
complex factorization at samples; g3 A1 with a sieved Λ-sum to
10⁵ against mpmath −ζ′/ζ within the integral tail bound; g4 A5
against both closed-form families at dps 30; g5 A4 + the R1
transform-sentence anchor; g6 the genericity counter-theorem at
two non-lattice pairs; g7 the four-predicate iff scan over
α ∈ {½; 0, ¼, ⅓, ¾}; g8 the paper's key sentences; g9 the
sibling chain (concentration_regrade 12/0, transitively the full
suite); g10 the footer census (67/1i–1aq). Footer advanced

seven sibling census gates advanced with their docstring
tellings, per-file with syntax checks (the wrapped-"66" variants

## Caveats

- The grammar is one choice; a different atom set changes densities. The atoms used are exactly
  the primitives the papers themselves use, which is the fairest available choice.
- Measurement σs are taken at the values used in `PREDICTIONS.md`; where the papers' σ accounting
  is disputed (e.g. the ℓ_A entry, where 301.44 vs 301.6±0.09 is −1.8σ, not the −0.16σ the table formerly

## Addendum 334 — the prose-only battery scoping (owner-commissioned)

**The commission.** "Let's stop running the full battery if there are only prose changes" — arriving after the round-218 batteries' cost was profiled for the owner (the full tower ~2 h solo and worse under contention; rounds 216, 217, and 218 each paid it; the measured hot spots are compute inside certified members, not anything a prose edit can reach).

**The rule (now codified in CLAUDE.md alongside the round-43 scoping).** A round's change set is PROSE-ONLY iff its diff touches no verifier bytes, no `tower_manifest.json`, and no gate semantics. For prose-only rounds the battery obligation is: the manifest-integrity precheck; a full run of the tower TOP verifier (its paper gates are the live sentries for the newest block, the needles, and the anchored census); and a full run of any older block-owning verifier whose text span the diff touches. The full tower remains obligatory at landings, certifications, code- or manifest-touching rounds, and after any battery failure. Sabotage suites always run live. Reviewer briefs state the classification; a reviewer who disputes it escalates the classification itself as a finding.

**The reasoning, recorded.** This is the cadence amendment's logic applied one level up: the amendment let a verifier attest its ANCESTORS by committed hash while recomputing its own claims; this scoping lets a REVIEW ROUND attest the unchanged tower by the same hash walk while recomputing everything the diff could have touched. A prose edit can break needles, censuses, and block claims — all gated by the top and block-owning verifiers, which still run in full. It cannot change what `cascade_heatflow_energy.py` computes; re-running that on a prose diff was ritual, and the round-43 precedent is explicit that ritual gets retired. Expected saving: ~2 h per prose-only round, which describes most convergence rounds.

**First application.** This very commit (CLAUDE.md + this record; no paper, no verifier, no manifest): battery obligation none beyond the precheck. Not applicable to the in-flight round-218 completion (its sweep touched thirteen verifier files and the manifest — the full 12/12 tower re-run stands, and is running) nor to convergence round 219 (same diff under review). The scoping first bites on the first prose-only sweep after 219.

**Standing state.** Round-218 batteries green — see Addendum 335. Convergence round 219 delivered — see Addendum 336.

## Addendum 341 — content-addressed compute checkpoints (owner-commissioned)

**The commission.** "When we commit the checkpoints could the file names include a sha of the script content / inputs so no calculations are repeated between runs or reviews?"

**The rule (codified in CLAUDE.md; helper `tools/research/ckpt_key.py`, committed this commit).** Checkpoint filenames embed sha256(script bytes + canonical inputs); state is reused only on byte-identical code and inputs. Three properties make this compatible with the evidence standard: (1) **self-invalidation** — a sabotage probe's code mangle changes the key, so a mangled tree can never reuse clean state and the observed censuses stay live; (2) **observability** — every run prints REUSED-with-key or RECOMPUTING, so a battery record always shows what was computed and what was attested; (3) **the landing-round fresh rule** — the hostile round on a new landing recomputes the new member with CASCADE_COMPUTE=fresh at least once, which is the run that validates the cache before anyone reuses it. Provenance (script sha, key, params) is stored inside each checkpoint file, and the wrapper's git history dates every state. Adoption: the upcoming 1bd verifier is the first consumer (its ~40-min spectrum stage becomes reusable across the clean run, the suite baseline, and tail-round batteries); the in-flight harvest keeps its plain-named files, which are cleaned at arc completion per A340.

**Standing state.** The 1bd harvest continues under the wrapper; the verifier will adopt ckpt_key at build.

## Addendum 372 — Stage B1 round 2 ("A"): the exact Temple optimizer; two instrument self-catches; the even frontier saturates at 0.80 while the odd sector reaches 1.05

**The commission.** "A" — the first of the four next moves offered at the B1-opening landing: Temple-objective-optimized trials with the ⟨Tφᵢ,Tφⱼ⟩ Gram.

**The method (`oneprime_push.py`).** The Kato–Temple value λ_T = ρ − σ²/(ℓ₂−ρ) is, in trial coefficients, the ratio (cᵀ(ℓ₂M − S)c)/(cᵀ(ℓ₂N − M)c) — so its exact maximizer over a whole trial subspace is the top eigenvector of that pencil, solved on the span where the denominator form is positive definite. This replaces S5's hand-picked trials with the best trial the subspace contains. The ℓ₂ stand-in is stress-tested as a three-rung ladder (combined-section λ₂, cos-24 λ₂, half-λ₂); the optimal vector's top-mode weight is reported as the truncation-exploit monitor.

**Two self-catches before any number landed.** (1) The first run's own gA gate stopped it at 1.45e-3: linear-edge modes have |ĝ| ~ 2w/r² sinc tails, so wide-grid truncation of ‖Tb‖² scales like w²log²R/R³ — and an optimizer would EXPLOIT underestimated high-mode S entries for fake σ² gains. Repair: frequencies capped, Rmax 6000→9000, raw-basis assembly with whitening as a linear map, gA re-aimed at the fam1 sub-block vs the certified build_Q64 matrix (tolerance 5e-4 = the certified instrument's own documented Rmax-600 truncation class, seen from the operator side). (2) The capped run's whitening reported dim 24 in the even sector: cos(πt/(2a)) × integer harmonics recombines EXACTLY into half-integer cosines — the p = 1 window family is fam1's own recombination, the union was degenerate, and the optimizer merely re-derived the cos-24 trial (Temple values matching S5 to 3 digits: the linear-edge 24-span is Temple-EXHAUSTED). Repair: NSM = 32 restores the genuinely new half-integer directions 24.5–32.5. Both catches are in the commit record (91397ce, 92be939, 8fc0e56) with the run-2 data preserved.

**The verdict (NSM = 32 / Rmax = 9000, eleven cells, gA 1.3e-4–4.4e-4).** The EVEN sector saturates at δ ≈ 0.80: +1.035e-3 at log 2 (the optimizer certifying S5's p1n32 trial as already optimal in its span), +2.1e-5 at 0.80 (the frontier), −4.6e-5 at 0.85 (σ factor 1.31 short), −4.6e-5 at 0.90 (factor 1.89) — and the enrichment bought only 7% of σ at 0.90, so the missing residual is NOT in the next harmonics: with S4's roughening trend the identified suspects are fractional edge exponents and/or much higher frequency, both requiring analytic tail corrections (the gA lesson applied forward). The ODD sector reaches 1.05: +2.1e-3 at 0.90 with the half-rung at +1.75e-3 (ROBUST — the round's first genuine advance past the S5 frontier), +1.6e-5 at 1.05 semi-robust (fails only the half-λ₂ stress), 1.09 non-robust (the ladder flagging it as designed). Standing: the full form Temple-closes at feasibility level on [log 2, 0.80] (even binding); σ/needed grows 0.50 → 9.9 across the even window, so no trial refinement alone reaches the top — past ~0.85 the route needs the fractional-edge/high-frequency trials with analytic tails, a different bound family (Lehmann–Goerisch), or the fallback verified-zeros chain. Still a survey, not a theorem (ℓ₂ stand-ins, float64 grids — the B1-opening scoping unchanged).

Lincei (9) Mat. Appl. 11 (2000), no. 3, 183-233 (2001); [2] "A variational approach to the explicit formula," Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 56 (2003), no. 8, 1151-1164. Its abstract's "Bombieri (2001, 2003)" = these two.
- Li, "A Hilbert-Schmidt integral operator and the Weil distribution" (arXiv:2404.13427, PDF references extracted): Bombieri cited once — Remarks I only.
- "A finite Guinand-Weil dictionary..." (arXiv:2607.02828v3, July 2026, PDF references extracted): Bombieri cited once — Remarks I only ([4], with EUDML link).
- bdim.eu complete tables of contents of Rend. Lincei (9) Mat. Appl. vol. 13 (2002), all three fascicles read: no such paper (the only Bombieri entry in the volume is Bombieri-Zannier, "A Note on squares in arithmetic progressions, II," pp. 69-75). A WebFetch summarizer HALLUCINATED a precise-looking citation ("Rend. Lincei 13 (2002), 13-57") for Part II during this sweep; the raw HTML of the same page, read directly, contains no such entry — recorded here as a methods warning: bibliographic claims from summarizing fetch tools must be verified against raw source bytes (Check-2 discipline applies to literature exactly as to the codebase).

**The de-facto Part II and what it contains.** Bombieri's continuation of Remarks I is the CPAM 2003 paper (dedicated to J. Moser). Its text is paywalled (Wiley returned metadata only; no open copy found via targeted searches); the sweep therefore rests on the per-theorem description in Suzuki 2606.09096, which maps it against Remarks I clause by clause: Problem B = the Rayleigh quotient on H^1_0(-a,a) ([1, Problem 1]); Problem A = L^2(E) over a finite union of intervals ([1, Problem 2]); Theorem 4.3 = minimizer existence ([1, Theorem 3]); Theorem 4.4 = the continuity claim ([1, Theorem 5]) — which Suzuki flags as "an analytically delicate issue" that "calls for a more careful analysis"; Sections 5-6 = Bombieri's Lagrangian ([1, Lemma 1]). All variational-qualitative. NO explicit support-length positivity threshold is attributed to either Bombieri paper anywhere in the accessible literature; small-a positivity is uniformly credited to Yoshida (1992, Lemma 2 — "sufficiently small," qualitative), and the explicit-threshold record to Connes-Consani (log 2). A 2003 CPAM paper holding a better explicit threshold than log 2 is irreconcilable with the entire 2021-2026 citation record celebrating CC's log 2 as the record; the conclusion stands on that unanimity even without the paywalled text.

**The July 2026 adjacent entrant, swept.** arXiv:2607.02828 ("A finite Guinand-Weil dictionary and archimedean tail order for the truncated Weil quadratic form," v3): works in the Connes-van Suijlekom / CCM GALERKIN-TRUNCATION frame (prime cutoff c > 1, frequency band N, all primes under the cutoff) — an exact zero-sum dictionary for the truncated form, a totally-positive archimedean tail increment, a two-sided certification budget B_T, and (notably) interval LDL^T factorization as a certification device. ## Addendum 388 — the tower pace retrofit (owner-commissioned: "The convergence tower is slowing the pace of research catastrophically"): the diagnosis was oversubscription, not compute; plus resume caching, zeros caching, bitwise-identical vectorization, and stage checkpoints

**The commission and the diagnosis.** The per-landing tower battery cost ~3 hours wall and a container restart discarded a 45-minute partial run. Measurement overturned the working theory: `cascade_heatflow_energy.py` ran **105 minutes in-tower vs 38 seconds standalone** (user 2m20s vs real 38 s) — the tower's 4 workers each spawned full-core BLAS thread pools, oversubscribing the box ~4x; and the mpmath zero pulls, initially suspected dominant, measure at ~0.1 s/zero. The heavy members' recorded in-tower times were contention artifacts, not compute.

**The five fixes (commits 8fd417b + this one):**
1. **run_tower resume cache** (8fd417b): each member's PASS recorded under sha256(member bytes) + sha256(manifest) + sha256(paper) — any honest input change invalidates; cached-vs-live census printed; TOWER_FRESH=1 forces live; failures never cached; run under the wrapper so the cache pushes every 10 minutes (git the only restore-proof storage).
2. **Thread pinning in run_tower**: each of the NW workers gets cpu_count/NW BLAS threads (OMP/OPENBLAS/MKL/NUMEXPR) — the single biggest lever, by measurement.
3. **`zeta_zeros_cache.py`**: the shared zero-ordinate cache with LIVE anchors — on every hit the first and last ordinates are recomputed at the same dps and must match exactly (mpmath deterministic; json round-trips float64 exactly); the consumers' own gates pin zero values downstream, so a poisoned cache cannot pass silently. Consumers: fluctuation (380@dps13), heatflow (60@dps20), prolate (260@dps15).
4. **Bitwise-identical vectorization** in `cascade_fluctuation_price.py` and `cascade_prolate_horizon.py`: the scalar 80-iteration `inv_Nbar` Newton loops (380 scalar calls per CUE try, up to 400 tries per conditioned point) replaced by the elementwise vector iteration, and the per-order `spherical_jn` loops by one broadcast call — both verified bitwise-identical before landing (the Newton iteration is elementwise; scipy evaluates each (n, z) pair identically either route). **RNG draw order untouched everywhere** — every seeded ensemble reproduces its recorded values exactly; no recorded observation changes.
5. **Stage checkpoints in `cascade_fluctuation_price.py`** (the floor_theory phase pattern, applied with the oneprime F248-5 lesson — gates NEVER sit behind the early-return): the expensive computed state (m120, the 26-point grid rows, the ten conditioned points) is byte-keyed on the member file; the g5 acceptance loop carries a per-point partial so a restart resumes at the last completed point (the deterministic seed ladder restarts per point, so a resumed point reproduces exactly). All gates run on loaded and fresh state alike.

**Not done, recorded as candidates:** stage checkpoints for `cascade_prolate_horizon.py` (its state includes complex eigenvectors — serialization surgery deferred; post-retrofit it is the tower's long pole at standalone scale) and any vectorization touching RNG draw order (never — it would silently re-draw the recorded ensembles).

## Addendum 417 — the two-prime window [log 3, log 4) opened (owner: "Start on the two-prime window"): Stage 0, the float64 feasibility reconnaissance — no counterexample; the Connes–Consani restoration at the prime 3 quantified; certification feasible at one odd cell only; the whole window Temple-hard

**The object.** The semi-local Weil form at the real place plus the primes 2 and 3. For test support length δ = 2a ∈ [log 3, log 4) the prime powers inside the autocorrelation window are exactly log 2 and log 3 (log 4 = 2 log 2 enters only past log 4; log 5 > log 4), so on that window the two-prime form **is** Weil's full quadratic functional, identically — the same identity Theorem 1bj(i) uses below log 3. Kernel W₂₃(r) = Re ψ(¼ + ir/2) − log π − C₂ cos(r log 2) − C₃ cos(r log 3), C_p = 2Λ(p)p^{−1/2} (C₂ = √2 log 2 the certified coefficient; C₃ = 2 log 3/√3 = 1.2685…; the normalisation read off the bridge's transcription of Connes–Consani eq. 2.6). In t-space the prime part is the pair of shifts −Σ_p (C_p/2)[b(t + log p) + b(t − log p)]; everything else is the committed one-prime t-space operator pipeline (`oneprime_fractional.py`, adjudicated at the cos-24 anchor), generalised by a primes list with the second kink at log 3 − a (`tools/research/twoprime_recon.py`, commits 54ad160/4d7df8f/a3101bb; checkpoints keyed on executable content).

**Faithfulness.** The continuity anchors reproduce Theorem 1bj's recorded float values: one-prime even 1.09 Temple −2.113e-5 (σ 1.910e-4), odd 1.09 +1.789e-5 — the numbers on the paper surface. At δ = 1.10 the two-prime and one-prime sections agree to three digits (λ₁ +5.997e-8 vs +6.003e-8 even; +1.434e-5 vs +1.414e-5 odd): the log 3 shift touches only a sliver of width δ − log 3 at the support edge, so continuity across log 3 holds and the prime-3 term's weight grows with δ.

**The Stage-0 table (float64, base 0.012; union span of harmonics + rough + fractional Gegenbauer edges; λ₁/λ₂ the section's own eigenvalues; Temple at the own-λ₂ rung / half rung).**

| δ | even λ₁ (two) | even λ₁ (one-prime, wrong form) | even Temple (two) | odd λ₁ (two) | odd λ₁ (one-prime) | odd Temple (two) own / half |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.10 | +6.0e-8 | +6.0e-8 | −2.5e-5 | +1.43e-5 | +1.41e-5 | **+1.17e-5 / +9.1e-6** |
| 1.12 | +3.4e-8 | +5.4e-8 | −4.4e-5 | +8.0e-6 | −1.3e-5 | **+4.9e-6 / +1.8e-6** |
| 1.13 | +2.6e-8 | +4.8e-8 | −5.7e-5 | +5.9e-6 | −5.2e-4 | +2.4e-6 / −1.1e-6 |
| 1.15 | +1.6e-8 | −2.9e-8 | −9.7e-5 | +3.2e-6 | −4.5e-2 | −7.8e-7 / −4.7e-6 |
| 1.20 | +7.2e-9 | −1.35e-3 | −4.3e-4 | +5.9e-7 | −1.54e-1 | −4.3e-6 |
| 1.25 | +6.3e-9 | −1.11e-2 | −2.3e-3 | +9.8e-8 | −2.53e-1 | −9.1e-6 |
| 1.30 | +5.2e-9 | −3.08e-2 | −1.4e-2 | +1.4e-8 | −3.44e-1 | −3.3e-5 |
| 1.35 | +4.6e-9 | −6.04e-2 | −7.3e-2 | −1.5e-9 | −4.29e-1 | −1.4e-4 |
| 1.38 | +4.1e-9 | −8.22e-2 | −2.7e-1 | −3.1e-9 | −4.76e-1 | −3.3e-4 |

(even λ₂ collapses 1.4e-3 → 2.0e-7 across the window; odd λ₂ 7.6e-2 → 3.8e-5; σ ≈ 1.3–2.3e-4 at every two-prime cell; the pipeline's block-CS residual mr ≈ 1e-5 throughout, as in the one-prime runs.)

**Findings.** *(1) No float64 counterexample.* The two-prime section's λ₁ is positive at every cell through 1.30 in both parities and at every even cell through 1.38; the two odd window-top readings (−1.5e-9 at 1.35, −3.1e-9 at 1.38) sit at the pipeline's own resolution — see the adjudication below — and the section λ₁ is in any case a variational upper bound on the true ground state, so a positive reading proves nothing and a negative one would need to survive refinement to mean anything. *(2) The Connes–Consani restoration at the prime 3, quantified.* CC's numerical remark (zeta-cycles, sec. 2.2 preamble) was that positivity is lost past a prime's threshold and restored by that prime's functional; the wrong-form diagnostic shows exactly this at p = 3: the one-prime form evaluated past log 3 turns negative within 0.02 of the threshold (even −2.9e-8 at 1.15; odd −1.3e-5 at 1.12) and reaches −0.34 (odd) / −0.06 (even) at 1.30–1.35, while the two-prime form stays positive at the 10⁻⁸–10⁻⁹ level — a cancellation of seven to eight orders of magnitude carried entirely by the C₃ cos(r log 3) term. The full form's ground state is continuous across the threshold (7.9e-8 at 1.09 → 6.0e-8 at 1.10) and decays monotonically toward the next threshold; the structure the one-prime window showed at its top (Theorem 1bj: "the even ground state is near-degenerate at the top of the window") is the whole two-prime window's condition. *(3) Certification feasibility.* Temple closes at the float level at **odd δ = 1.10 and 1.12** (own and half rungs both positive) and at odd 1.13 on the own rung only; it fails at every even cell (σ ≈ 2e-4 against λ₁ ≈ 10⁻⁸: the ratio σ/λ₁ ≈ 10⁴ that made the one-prime even top Temple-hard now holds across the even window) and at every odd cell beyond 1.13. The even sector's λ₂ collapses toward λ₁ (7e-7 at 1.35, 2e-7 at 1.38: a near-degenerate pair at the bottom of the spectrum), which removes the Temple premise ℓ₂ altogether near log 4 — no trial span can repair a vanishing spectral gap; certifying the window top needs a different lower-bound principle than Kato–Temple. *(4) The kernel.* W₂₃'s negative set on [0, 260] is six pieces of total length 11.64 (against W₂'s two pieces, 6.89), minimum −7.62 at r = 0: the Birman–Schwinger counting support of a Stage 1 roughly doubles.

**Stage 0b — the window-top adjudication (bases 0.012 / 0.008 / 0.005 on the six cells δ ∈ {1.30, 1.35, 1.38} × parity).** Producer `stability()` in `twoprime_recon.py` (commit a3101bb; checkpoint af7b10b). λ₁ by base 0.012 / 0.008 / 0.005 — even 1.30: +5.17e-9 / +6.14e-9 / +4.97e-9; even 1.35: +4.59e-9 / +5.89e-9 / +4.84e-9; even 1.38: +4.08e-9 / +5.71e-9 / +4.77e-9; odd 1.30: +1.41e-8 / +1.64e-8 / +1.76e-8; **odd 1.35: −1.45e-9 / +6.12e-10 / +1.68e-9; odd 1.38: −3.11e-9 / −1.05e-9 / −8.9e-11.** *Verdict:* the two negatives are quadrature — both move monotonically through or toward zero under refinement, while the even cells scatter by ±1e-9 across the same bases with λ₂ unchanged to four digits (7.03e-7, 2.00e-7), which fixes the pipeline's λ₁ floor at ~10⁻⁹. No counterexample; the honest statement for the window top is that the odd ground state at δ = 1.38 is **0 ± 10⁻⁹** — the full form's positivity margin touches zero, at this resolution, 0.006 below the log 4 threshold where the next prime power (2², coefficient log 2) enters. σ also carries a quadrature component (2.3e-4 → 9.6e-5 at base 0.005 on the even cells; 1.1e-4 → 4.4e-5 odd), so Temple values improve with refinement but remain two to five orders from closing at any cell beyond 1.13. *Structural reading (measured, not derived):* across both certified windows the full form's ground state on maximal support decays toward zero as the support approaches the next prime-power threshold — 1e-3 at log 2⁺ → 8e-8 at log 3⁻ (Theorem 1bj's even top) → 6e-8 at log 3⁺ → 0 ± 1e-9 at log 4⁻ — with the missing prime's functional restoring it past each threshold; whether the margin vanishes *exactly* at each threshold is a question the interval instruments could address at the one-prime top (log 3⁻) before the two-prime top.

**What the arc owes next (task list; owner's choice of order).** Stage 1: the certified Birman–Schwinger counts for W₂₃ at the feasible odd cells (1.10, 1.12) — the same instrument with the second cosine and the doubled support; Stage 2: the interval kernel enclosure (second cosine; derivative majorants gain C₃ log 3 and C₃ log² 3) and the closed-form operator (second shift, second kink) for the Temple certificates at those cells, then a Theorem 1bk landing with honest scope (odd sector at the bottom of the window only; the even sector and the window top open and, near log 4, structurally beyond Temple). Checks 7/8 clean (classical machinery throughout; Riemann-side pure mathematics, no hypothesis input). **No RH consequence is claimed**; the Stage-0 numbers are float64 reconnaissance, not certificates.

## Addendum 418 — the structural question (owner: "The structural question first pls"): does the full form's ground-state margin vanish at a prime-power threshold? The analytic half: no, under RH the margin is strictly positive at every finite support length, thresholds included (Beurling sampling); unconditionally the full form has no jump at a threshold — only the truncated form does. The measured half: the margin curve λ₁(δ) across three regimes

**The question, stated exactly.** Let Q be Weil's full quadratic functional and, for a support length δ = 2a, let λ₁(δ) be the bottom of the spectrum of Q compressed to test functions supported in [−a, a] with the L²[−a, a] normalisation (the instruments' Rayleigh quotient ⟨b, Tb⟩/⟨b, b⟩; the section values on the committed spans are variational upper bounds on it). The Stage-0 numbers (A417) showed λ₁ decaying toward the pipeline floor as δ approached log 4, and Theorem 1bj's even top showed the same approach toward log 3. The question: is λ₁(log p^k) = 0 at a threshold — does the margin *touch zero* exactly where the next prime power enters?

**(i) Monotonicity, rigorous.** λ₁(δ) is non-increasing in δ: for a < a′, extension by zero embeds L²[−a, a] isometrically in L²[−a′, a′] and Q is one fixed form on compactly supported functions (its "semi-local" expressions on each window are identities, Theorem 1bj(i) and A417), so the infimum over the larger domain is no larger. The paper's nesting argument in Theorem 1bj(ii) is this statement.

**(ii) No jump at a threshold, unconditionally.** On [log p − ε, log p + ε] the full form differs from the previous window's form by the incoming shift −(C_p/2)⟨b, b(· + log p) + b(· − log p)⟩, which acts only on the sliver |t| ∈ [log p − a, a] of width 2a − log p → 0 at the threshold; its contribution is bounded by C_p‖b‖·‖b·1_sliver‖, and a unit-norm b concentrated on a shrinking sliver pays the archimedean kernel's log-growth (W(r) ~ log r on the bandwidth 1/width it must occupy), so the infimum is carried by functions on which the sliver term vanishes with the width. The full form's λ₁ therefore passes a threshold continuously; what is discontinuous in its *behaviour* is the **truncated** form — the previous window's operator continued past its threshold — which is what Connes–Consani observed numerically at both thresholds (zeta-cycles sec. 2.2 for p = 2; sec. 2.4, "failure past log 3 when p = 3's contribution is withheld", as the bridge's anchor A2 records it) and what A417's diagnostic quantified on this pipeline (the one-prime form at δ = 1.30: odd −0.34; the full form there: +1.4×10⁻⁸). Measured: λ₁ even 7.9×10⁻⁸ at 1.09 (one-prime) and 6.0×10⁻⁸ at 1.10 (two-prime); odd 1.95×10⁻⁵ → 1.43×10⁻⁵ — continuous to the resolution, and the curve below carries the full picture across log 2 as well.

**(iii) Strict positivity at every finite δ under RH — thresholds are not special.** Weil's explicit formula (classical; the instruments' Q is Connes–Consani's semi-local form, eq. 2.11 of the zeta-cycles paper, by the bridge's certified dictionary — `oneprime_bridge.py`, gates G0–G4 — and that form is the explicit formula's quadratic version) writes Q(g) as the sum over zeros of f̂(ρ) with f = g ⋆ g̃; under RH every ρ = ½ + iγ with γ real and f̂(ρ) = |ĝ(γ)|², so Q(g) = Σ_γ |ĝ(γ)|² (with multiplicity), and ĝ is an entire function of exponential type a (Paley–Wiener). The zeros have counting function N(T) ~ (T/2π) log(T/2π), hence contain uniformly separated subsets of arbitrarily large Beurling density; by Beurling's sampling theorem for the Paley–Wiener space PW_a (a separated real set of lower uniform density exceeding a/π is a set of sampling), there is c(δ) > 0 with Σ_γ |ĝ(γ)|² ≥ c(δ)‖ĝ‖² for every g supported in [−a, a]. Hence **under RH, λ₁(δ) ≥ c(δ) > 0 for every finite δ** — the margin never vanishes, at a threshold or anywhere else; the sampling constant decays as the support (the exponential type) grows, which is the decay the curve measures. The weaker statement — no *nonzero* g with Q(g) = 0, from Jensen's bound n(T) = O(T) on the zeros of an exponential-type function against N(T) ≫ T — is the same argument without the uniformity. Unconditionally the only thing a threshold does is make the *previous* truncation wrong; if RH fails, λ₁(δ) turns negative at some finite δ, and nothing ties that δ to a prime power.

**(iv) What is certifiable, and what would close the odd sector's question at log 3 rigorously.** Domain nesting makes a certified positive lower bound at any δ′ > log 3 a certified positive lower bound at log 3 itself: a Kato–Temple certificate at the two-prime odd cell δ = 1.10 (Stage-0 float Temple +1.17×10⁻⁵, half rung +9.1×10⁻⁶ — the feasible cell) would state **λ₁(log 3) ≥ Temple(odd 1.10) > 0 in the odd sector**, unconditionally: the margin at the log 3 threshold is bounded away from zero, and by (i) so is the entire one-prime window's odd margin. That is the first two-prime certificate and the rigorous form of the structural answer for the odd sector in one object; it is Stage 1/2 at one cell. The even sector's version is out of reach of Temple at its top (Theorem 1bj's honest scope; the two-prime even cells are all Temple-hard), and the certified even bracket stands at [2.68×10⁻⁷ (Temple), ρ] at δ = 1.0.

**(v) The measured half — the margin curve (`tools/research/twoprime_margin.py`, commit 4b914e5; base 0.008; both parities; the full form per regime on δ ∈ [0.50, 1.386) in steps of 0.02 plus the threshold-adjacent points; the wrong form at the first points past each threshold).** Checkpoint 73e7a60; 100 cells.

*Continuity at both thresholds:* across log 2 (0.69 → 0.70) even 1.385e-3 → 1.194e-3 and odd 7.79e-2 → 6.55e-2, the full form and the previous regime's form agreeing to two digits at the first point past the threshold (the sliver is 0.007 wide); across log 3 (1.09 → 1.10) even 7.89e-8 → 5.97e-8, odd 1.95e-5 → 1.43e-5 — no jump anywhere, as (ii) says. *The wrong form's divergence:* four grid steps past each threshold the previous truncation has already separated by an order of magnitude (arch form at 0.74: odd 4.5e-3 against the full 3.6e-2) or changed sign (one-prime form at 1.14: odd −2.2e-2 against the full +4.3e-6), which is Connes–Consani's sec. 2.2/2.4 phenomenon on a grid. *The decay law (least squares of log₁₀ λ₁ on δ, full form, above the floor):* even 7.5 decades per unit δ on the archimedean regime (rms 0.03), 10.9 on the one-prime window (rms 0.09); odd 3.7 (arch), 9.2 (one-prime), **15.0 on the two-prime window** (rms 0.04, 12 points to 1.32) — the log-slope steepens window by window, so the margin's decay is faster than exponential in δ; the even two-prime regime is floor-limited (its λ₁ flattens at 5.5–7×10⁻⁹ from δ ≈ 1.18, a positive quadrature bias, so the even margin beyond 1.18 is *unresolved at this base* and only bounded above by ~6×10⁻⁹), and the odd sector reaches the floor at δ ≈ 1.34 (2.1×10⁻⁹, then −2×10⁻¹⁰, −1.1×10⁻⁹, −1.2×10⁻⁹ — the noise band established at Stage 0b). *The spectral gap:* the even λ₂ collapses from 1.4×10⁻³ at 1.10 to 1.6×10⁻⁷ at 1.386 — the even ground state becomes part of a near-degenerate pair at the bottom of the spectrum, which is why no Temple trial can reach the even top (A417); the odd gap stays four orders wider. *Answer, measured:* the margin does not vanish at log 2 or log 3 — it is 1.2×10⁻³/6.5×10⁻² (even/odd) at log 2 and 6×10⁻⁸/1.4×10⁻⁵ at log 3, continuous through both — and its approach to zero before log 4 is the tail of a super-exponential decay that reaches the pipeline's 10⁻⁹ resolution around δ ≈ 1.2 (even) and 1.34 (odd), not a threshold effect; (iii) says it is positive there under RH, and nothing measured contradicts that.

**Standing state.** The structural question is answered at the theorem level (iii) and at the measured level (v); the rigorous odd-sector answer at log 3 is one certificate away (iv) and is the same object as the two-prime arc's first landing. Checks 7/8 clean (Paley–Wiener, Beurling sampling, Jensen, Weil's explicit formula — classical throughout; no hypothesis input; Riemann-side pure mathematics). **No RH consequence is claimed**: (iii) is a consequence *of* RH, stated as such.

**Stage 1/2 reconnaissance (`twoprime_odd_recon.py`, float64).** *The count row is feasible* in the one-prime instrument's shape: the odd-projected pole-free count ≤ 1 holds to ν = 0.08 at β = 1.5 (margin 2.6e-3), ν = 0.07 at β = 1.3 (2.9e-3); the tail lemma h₊(rmax) − C₂ − C₃ > ν + β needs rmax = 600 for β ≥ 1.5 (h₊(260) − C₂ − C₃ = 1.47; h₊(600) − C₂ − C₃ = 2.31). *The two-stage odd route fails here.* The interval Temple instrument evaluates entire trials only; the pure-harmonic odd basis (24 integer + 24 half-integer sines; whitened dimension 27) has σ = 6.3e-4 at ρ = 1.437e-5, and the two-stage route's premise — ℓ₂ = ν₁ ≤ λ₁(PWP_odd) ≈ 0.0149 by interlacing, ν₁ ≈ 0.011 after the pole-free Temple — needs σ ≤ 3.9e-4: Temple −2.3e-5 at both count rows. The ν = 3/2 Gegenbauer polynomial modes add nothing (they vanish at the edge as the integer sines do; whitened dimension unchanged); Stage 0's closure at this cell came from the non-entire fractional-edge modes (weight 0.60) and from using the full section's λ₂ = 0.076 as the rung, neither admissible in a certificate. *The device that works is the odd analogue of Theorem 1bj's even-top device: the pole-inclusive count.* For the odd sector the pole is the negative rank-one −2|χ⟩⟨χ|, χ = sinh(t/2), so T_odd − ν = max(W₂₃ − ν, β)(D) − [qt(D) + 2|χ⟩⟨χ|] and Weyl monotonicity gives #{T_odd < ν} ≤ #{eig(qt(D) + 2|χ⟩⟨χ|) > β}: the pole enters the counting operator with a *positive* sign, so its frame Gram is a genuine Gram bordered by the pole column — closed-form entries b_i = √c_i·2∫₀^a sin(r_i t) sinh(t/2) dt = √c_i [J(½) − J(−½)](r_i), corner ⟨g, g⟩ = 2(sinh a − a) = 0.0563 — and the one-prime verified eigen-enclosure applies directly, with no Woodbury secular certificate and no count-regime gate (the even sector's devices, where the pole enters negatively). The certificate then bounds λ₂(T_odd) ≥ ν* directly and the Temple is single-stage. *The row.* The pole costs ≈ 0.045 in μ₂ (its strength); at β = 1.5 the pole-inclusive count holds only to ν = 0.03, where the harmonic Temple closes by 3% in σ (+1.1e-6) — too thin for interval slop; at β = 2.0 (support 86, ~4,400 Simpson nodes, last piece ending at r = 435 < rmax = 600) it holds through ν = 0.045 with margin 1.4e-2, falling 4.8e-3 per 0.005 in ν, so **(ν*, β, rmax) = (0.05, 2.0, 600)** with a float margin ≈ 9e-3; the harmonic Temple at ℓ₂ = 0.05 is +6.4e-6 (needed σ 8.5e-4 against 6.3e-4). At β = 2.5 (rmax 1000, ~7,400 nodes) the margins are wider still (3.4e-2 / 2.9e-2 / 2.4e-2 at ν = 0.035 / 0.04 / 0.045) — held in reserve. ## Addendum 420 — the zero side of the margin curve (owner: "Can we derive the zero side heuristic?" / "can we extract a proof?"): the explicit-formula identity computed from 3,000 zeros reproduces the prime-side λ₁(δ) to 0.1–0.5%, extends the curve six decades past the log 4 wall, explains the prime-side pipeline's floor, and reads off the decay law s/eᵟ ≈ 4.8 decades per unit — a research probe, conditional, no proof extracted

**The identity (classical; Weil's explicit formula on the autocorrelation).** For real g supported on [−a, a], h = g∗g̃, G(s) = ∫g(t)e^{(s−½)t}dt: Σ_ρ G(ρ)G(1−ρ) = (1/2π)∫|ĝ|²[Re ψ(¼+ir/2) − log π]dr − Σ_{p^k} (2 log p/p^{k/2}) h(log p^k) ± 2⟨χ,g⟩², the right side being the paper's semi-local form Q(g) with every prime power inside the window — the full functional. Under RH the left side is Σ_γ|ĝ(γ)|², so **λ₁(δ) = min_{‖g‖=1, supp ⊂ [−a,a]} Σ_γ|ĝ(γ)|²**: the same number the prime-side pipeline computes, with no prime and no window in sight. Unconditionally the identity holds but the zero-side terms of a hypothetical off-line pair are 2 Re[G(ρ)G(1−ρ)] of unbounded sign over the test space, so the zero side yields window positivity only under RH (or per fixed smooth g, from the verified zeros); the prime side remains the only unconditional route — the answer to "can we extract a proof": no, and the reason is Weil's equivalence itself.

**The instrument (`tools/research/zeroside_margin.py`, float64, a research probe: not a tower member, not cited by the paper, NOT a certificate).** Ground state of the Gram 2Σ_{n≤N} ĝ_i(γ_n)ĝ_j(γ_n) in the 27/28-function integer + half-integer cosine/sine basis per parity (non-orthogonal: generalised eigenproblem against the mass matrix, whitened at 10⁻¹⁰), N = 3,000 zeros (mpmath `zetazero`, cached at `checkpoints/zeta_zeros_3000.txt`, γ₃₀₀₀ = 3533.33), the tail beyond γ_N by the Riemann–von Mangoldt density integral to 5×10⁴ and the edge asymptotic past it (tail share 0.1–1.3% at every resolved cell; the no-tail value differs by ≤ 1.3%). Compared against the committed prime-side curve (`twoprime_margin_b0f7c8ea0f80`, the right regime per δ).

**Result — the cross-check.** | δ | even zeros / primes | odd zeros / primes | — 0.5: 3.3364e-2 / 3.3361e-2, 4.0895e-1 / 4.0893e-1; 0.7: 1.1943e-3 / 1.1938e-3, 6.5490e-2 / 6.5484e-2; 0.9: 1.6199e-5 / 1.6178e-5, 2.4110e-3 / 2.4074e-3; 1.0: 9.3693e-7 / 9.4063e-7, 1.9461e-4 / 1.9406e-4; 1.1: 5.3407e-8 / 5.9672e-8, **1.4403e-5 / 1.4337e-5** (Theorem 1bk's cell: the certified Temple 6.3136e-6 ≤ ρ = 1.4373e-5, and the zero side's 1.4403e-5 sits 0.2% above the prime-side float section, as an upper-sampled minimum should); 1.2: 1.6264e-9 / 7.7366e-9, 6.0427e-7 / 5.9747e-7; 1.3: 4.0299e-11 / 6.1435e-9, 1.8702e-8 / 1.6439e-8; log 4: 7.8471e-13 / 5.4690e-9, 4.9603e-10 / −1.1561e-9. λ₂ agrees likewise (1.0: 1.807e-2 / 1.80e-2; 1.1 odd: 7.605e-2 / 7.56e-2). *The prime-side floor explained:* A418 recorded the even curve flattening at ≈ 6×10⁻⁹ past δ ≈ 1.2 as "unresolved at this base" and the odd values at the window top as quadrature noise at ±10⁻⁹; the zero side shows the true even margin is 1.6×10⁻⁹ at 1.2, 4×10⁻¹¹ at 1.3, 8×10⁻¹³ at log 4 — the prime-side plateau was its GL-panel quadrature floor, and the +10% even excess at 1.1 (5.97 vs 5.34 ×10⁻⁸) is that same floor added to a value only ten times larger; the odd window-top negatives were the floor's sign noise around a true +5×10⁻¹⁰. *Beyond the wall:* even 3.8×10⁻¹⁵ at 1.5 (at the float64 floor; flagged), odd 3.5×10⁻¹² at 1.5 and 1.8×10⁻¹⁴ at 1.6 (resolved; tail shares 1.2–1.3%); at 1.6 even and beyond the Gram's float64 noise (10⁻¹⁶) dominates and the probe flags the cells. The zero side has no window: δ = 1.5 and 1.6 lie in the [log 4, log 5) window whose prime-side form (2, 3, 4) the pipeline never built.

**Result — the profile and the decay law.** The share of the ground state's form carried by γ₁ falls from 0.43/0.81 (even/odd) at δ = 0.5 to < 10⁻³ at 1.1; at δ ≥ 1.2 the first three zeros carry nothing and half the form sits above zero #10–22 (γ ≈ 50–83), 90% above #90–160 (γ ≈ 220–334): the minimiser learns to vanish at the low zeros and its residual is leakage onto the mid zeros — the mechanism of the super-exponential decay. The slope s(δ) = −d log₁₀λ₁/dδ between successive cells, divided by eᵟ: even 3.7, 4.2, 3.9, 4.5, 4.8, 4.4, 4.8, 4.6, 5.2 (δ = 0.55 … 1.34; last three mean 4.87); odd 1.5, 2.8, 3.1, 3.4, 4.2, 4.0, 4.4, 4.3, 4.8, 4.5, 4.9 (δ = 0.55 … 1.55; last three mean 4.71). **Read off, not derived: s/eᵟ → ≈ 4.8 decades per unit of eᵟ for both parities, i.e. ln λ₁(δ) ≈ −11·eᵟ + const at the top of the resolved range** (the odd ratio still rising slowly; a δ·eᵟ law fits worse — its ratio falls monotonically from 6.7 to 3.4). The counting heuristic behind the form (at the effective height T₀ = 2πeᵟ the type-a degrees of freedom below it number δT₀/π = 2δeᵟ, the zeros ±γ below it ≈ (T₀/π)log(T₀/2πe) = 2(δ−1)eᵟ, excess 2eᵟ; T₀ is where the excess is maximal) predicts the eᵟ scaling; its Landau–Widom constant does not fit at these Shannon numbers (c ≈ 3–8) and the constant here is empirical. *Consequence for the programme (a forecast, conditional):* the margin at the window of prime p scales like 10^{−4.8p}: ≈ 10⁻¹⁴ at log 5 (measured 1.8×10⁻¹⁴ odd at 1.6), ≈ 10⁻²⁴ at log 7, ≈ 10⁻²⁹ at log 8 — every window past the second prime is beyond double-precision interval certification, and a multiprecision certificate at log 5 would need ≈ 20 digits of headroom on every enclosure. The arc's stop at the two-prime window is where the decay law says it must stop.

**Standing state.** The zero-side identity is verified as a computation (the primes-2-and-3 operator and 3,000 zeros produce the same spectrum to the prime-side pipeline's resolution); the decay law is measured, conditional on the zeros used being on the line (they are: verified), and it is a forecast about certificates, not a theorem. Nothing here is a paper surface; the probe is committed for reproducibility only. Checks 7/8 clean (Weil's explicit formula, Paley–Wiener, IEEE-754 — classical; no hypothesis input; Riemann-side pure mathematics). **No RH consequence is claimed; no proof was extracted, and the reason is recorded above.**

## Addendum 421 — a mechanism hypothesised for the decay law (owner: "Hypothesise a mechanism"): Beurling threshold + Slepian concentration — the ground state is Slepian's ψ₀ on a sub-threshold interval, vanishing exactly at the zeta zeros below the threshold, and the margin is its leakage caught by the supra-threshold zeros; tested on the zero-side ground states (overlap 0.9999; zeros coincident), conditional and heuristic

**The hypothesis.** Write T₀(δ) = 2πeᵟ. For exponential type a = δ/2 the zeros' density (1/2π)log(x/2π) exceeds the Nyquist density a/π exactly for x > T₀, so (Beurling) the zeros above T₀ form a sampling set for Paley–Wiener functions of type a while those below are sub-Nyquist and can be interpolated freely. The minimiser of Σ_γ|ĝ(γ)|² therefore (i) concentrates ĝ on an interval [−T_eff, T_eff] with T_eff ≲ T₀ — the most concentrated function of type a on an interval is Slepian's prolate ψ₀ (even) / ψ₁ (odd), with concentration parameter c = a·T_eff; (ii) places exact zeros at the zeta zeros below T₀ (cheap: sub-Nyquist); (iii) pays the prolate's leakage 1 − λ₀(c) ≈ 4√(πc)·e^{−2c} (Slepian–Fuchs) on the sampling set above T₀, where a fixed fraction of the leaked mass is caught. Hence **ln λ₁(δ) ≈ −2c + ½ln c + const with c ≈ θ·πδeᵟ, θ = T_eff/T₀ ∈ (0.6, 1)** — the eᵟ law of A420 with the coefficient 2πθ(1+δ) nats per unit eᵟ, and the super-exponential steepening because T₀ itself grows like eᵟ.

**The tests (even sector; `zeroside_margin.py --prolate`, the committed mode `zeroside_margin.py --prolate 3000 0.8 1.0 1.2 1.386 1.5 1.6` reproduces the session's five cells digit-for-digit and adds the sixth).** (1) *Prolate shape:* the overlap of the zero-side ground state's ĝ with ψ₀(c = aT₀) on [−T₀, T₀] is 0.9998, 0.9982, 0.9953, 0.9914, 0.9855 at δ = 0.8, 1.0, 1.2, log 4, 1.5, and with the prolate on the best-fit interval it is **0.9999–1.0000 at every δ** — the ground state IS a prolate; the best-fit interval T_eff = 13.3, 14.5, 15.6, 17.6, 18.3 = 0.95, 0.85, 0.75, 0.70, 0.65 T₀. (2) *Mass:* 99.93–100.00% of ĝ's Plancherel mass lies inside [−T₀, T₀]. (3) *Zeros:* ĝ's real zeros in (0, T₀) are exactly the zeta zeros below T₀ — none at δ = 0.8 (T₀ = 14.0 < γ₁); {14.1} at 1.0 and 1.2; {14.1, 21.0, 25.0} at log 4 and 1.5 — coincident to the print precision (0.1). (4) *The leakage formula:* with c = aT₀ (θ = 1) the model ln[4√(πc)e^{−2c}] against the measured ln λ₁ (even): −2.75/−3.40, −6.15/−6.73, −10.98/−11.03, −14.05/−13.88, −17.63/−16.75, −21.81/−20.24, −26.66/−23.93, −31.44/−27.87, −38.76/−33.19 at δ = 0.5, 0.7, 0.9, 1.0, 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, log 4, 1.5 — within one nat through δ = 1.1 with no free constant, then the measured value runs less negative by 1.6, 2.7, 3.6, 5.6 nats as the count of zeros below T₀ rises 1 → 2 → 3 → 3 and T_eff/T₀ falls (the enforced zeros are not free: each shortens the concentration interval); the odd sector with ψ₁'s leakage (n = 1 in the Slepian–Fuchs prefactor) fits to 1–2 nats through 1.0 and drifts likewise. The measured/model ratio of ln λ₁ is θ ≈ 0.93, 0.89, 0.86 at δ = 1.2, log 4, 1.5, matching the fitted T_eff/T₀ trend.

**Predictions the hypothesis makes (testable on the zero side without new machinery).** (a) A new exact zero of the ground state appears whenever a zeta zero crosses T₀: γ₄ = 30.42 at δ = ln(γ₄/2π) = 1.577, γ₅ = 32.94 at 1.655, γ₆ = 37.59 at 1.787. **Confirmed on the committed run's added cell:** at δ = 1.6 (T₀ = 31.1) the even ground state's zeros in (0, T₀) are {14.1, 21.0, 25.0, 30.4} against the zeta zeros {14.1, 21.0, 25.0, 30.4} — the fourth zero present, as predicted, in a cell whose λ₁ itself sits at the float64 floor (the eigenvector's structure survives where its eigenvalue does not); overlap with the best-fit prolate 0.9998 at T_eff = 0.60 T₀ (the scan's lower bound — the true T_eff there may be smaller). (b) The decay slope in nats is 2πθ(1+δ)eᵟ with θ drifting slowly downward — A420's measured s/eᵟ (4.4–5.2 decades = 10–12 nats at δ ≈ 1–1.35 against 2π(1+δ) = 12.6–14.7 nats) gives θ_slope ≈ 0.80–0.82, consistent with the fitted interval ratio. (c) The profile: ψ₀'s leakage beyond the edge falls like 1/x², so the caught form's median sits near 2–3 T₀ and its 90% point near 10 T₀ — A420 measured the median at γ ≈ 50–83 (2.4–3.0 T₀) and 90% at γ ≈ 220–334 (9–12 T₀). (d) Parity: the odd/even ratio of margins should grow like 8c ∝ δeᵟ; measured ln(λ₁^odd/λ₁^even) = 2.5, 4.0, 5.0, 5.3, 5.6, 5.9, 6.1, 6.4, 6.8 at δ = 0.5 … 1.5, against ln(8c_eff) = 3.7–4.7: the growth is there, the level is ~2 nats high (the even sector's positive pole term and the odd sector's negative one are not in the prolate model).

**Status.** A hypothesis with four confirmations (shape, mass, zeros, one-nat agreement of the leakage formula through δ = 1.1 with no fitted constant) and one systematic residual (the cost of the enforced zeros, growing with their count) — a mechanism, not a theorem: Beurling's sampling theorem and Slepian's asymptotics are classical, but the identification of the minimiser with ψ₀ is empirical here and the leakage-capture constant is not derived. Everything sits on the zero side (conditional as A420 records). *What it would take to make it a theorem:* an upper bound λ₁(δ) ≤ Q(ψ₀-trial) is immediate and unconditional (any trial works, and Q is computed on the prime side); a matching lower bound needs a quantitative Beurling constant on the zeros above T₀ — under RH. Checks 7/8 clean (Beurling, Slepian–Fuchs, Weil's explicit formula — classical; no hypothesis input; Riemann-side pure mathematics). **No RH consequence is claimed.**

**Prior art within the program — a correction to this addendum's framing (lead-noticed the same day, before any review; record files are corrected when noticed).** The threshold T₀ = 2πeᵟ is NOT new to A420–A421: it is the paper's **dodging horizon**, stated in Theorem 1az(v) ("A support-δ function can only place zeros at ζ-zeros below T ≈ 2πe^δ (type capacity vs zero density — classical Paley–Wiener/Jensen reasoning)"), tested and refuted-then-measured in Theorems 1ba and 1bb ("the capacity edge of Slepian sections IS the Paley–Wiener horizon, measured"; the 1/c march to 2πe⁴), with the **uniform dodger** (the minimiser suppressing |f̂(γ_k)|² at the first zeros) in 1az(iii) and the Slepian-optimal basis in 1bb(ii). The zero-side K-zero section as an instrument is 1az(iv)'s rate instrument. A421's hypothesis therefore rediscovered the program's own horizon in the zero-side coordinates, and its author (this session) had not re-read 1az–1bb before claiming a mechanism — a Check-0/Check-4 process defect on the lead's side, recorded as such. **What A420–A421 add beyond 1az–1bb, restated narrowly:** (a) the zero-side ground state reproduces the *prime-side pipeline's* λ₁(δ) across the archimedean, one-prime, and two-prime regimes to 0.1–0.5% (A420's cross-check against `twoprime_margin`), explains that pipeline's 6×10⁻⁹ floor, and extends the δ-curve six decades past log 4 — 1az measured the decay in n at fixed δ (c(δ)), not the full margin's decay in δ; (b) the decay law in δ read off as s/eᵟ ≈ 4.8 decades per unit; (c) the identification of the minimiser itself with Slepian's ψ₀ on a sub-horizon interval (overlap 0.9999; T_eff/T₀ = 0.95 → 0.60 measured), with its exact zeros at the sub-horizon zeta zeros, and the Slepian–Fuchs leakage formula matching ln λ₁ to one nat through δ = 1.1 with no fitted constant — 1bb used prolates as a *basis* and measured the horizon as the capacity edge; it did not identify the minimiser with ψ₀ or price the margin by ψ₀'s leakage. The "Predictions" paragraph stands as written; the word "hypothesis" in the heading should be read as "the horizon's leakage-pricing, hypothesised".

## Addendum 422 — the tile investigated (owner: "Pack the infinite unit ball" → "Investigate the tile"): the semi-local tile's tightness — each S-local form stays positive past its own window by a slack that shrinks with every prime, the odd sector fails first, and the failure is the edge-mass tradeoff Q_full(c) − Q_q(c); the archimedean form's positivity outlasts Connes–Consani's log 2 window by 7–17%

**The tile, in the paper's terms.** Theorem 1as builds the adelic self-dual vector Φ = e^(−πx²)·Π 1_{ℤ_p} — the Gaussian occupant of the infinite unit ball at ∞ and the p-adic unit balls at the finite places — whose self-pairings are the Euler factors ("ζ is the outer product of unit-ball self-pairings"). The tiling ℚ + ([0,1) × Π ℤ_p) = 𝔸 has covolume one, and Poisson summation for Φ over it is Tate's functional equation: the first-order packing statement, unconditional. Weil's form is the tiling's second-order statement, and its smooth side is the cascade's own potential on the critical line: from Theorem 1ao's d/ds ln B(s) = p(s−1) + 1/s, **W_∞(r) = Re ψ(¼ + ir/2) − log π = 2·Re p(−½ + ir)** exactly (verified to 20 digits at r = 3.7), with the pole term the 1/s ladder of the same unit-ball factor; the discrete side is the p-adic balls' pairings differentiated (the von Mangoldt sum). "The discrete never overfills the smooth" is then: the p-adic unit balls' pairings never exceed the archimedean ball's potential plus its pole ladder on any probe — Bochner positive-definiteness of the Weil distribution, whose Fourier transform is the zero measure; Weil's criterion; RH. The paper's 1az(vii) records where the sphere-packing analogy stops ("the Weil optimum collapses to the boundary").

**The semi-local tile and its window.** The tile with the finite places S = {p ≤ P} defines the S-local form Q_S; on support lengths below the next prime-power lag log q it IS the full functional (Theorems 1bj(i), 1bk(i)), and past log q it is the wrong form. *The question investigated:* how tight is the tile — does Q_S lose positivity as soon as its window ends (the prime q arriving exactly when needed), or does it carry slack? Measured with the float64 reconnaissance operator generalised to arbitrary (lag, weight) terms (`tools/research/tile_tightness.py`; base 0.012; the one-prime odd cell at 1.10 reproducing A417's recorded 1.41376×10⁻⁵ and the two-prime 1.4341×10⁻⁵ digit-for-digit), sixty cells: per parity, λ₁^S(δ) past the window's end at δ = log q + ε, together with the decomposition on the S-ground state c_S — **λ₁^S = Q_full(c_S) − Q_q(c_S)**, Q_q the missing term's form (= −C_q·h_c(log q), h the autocorrelation) — and the edge mass g(a)²/‖g‖². Results (`checkpoints/tile_tightness_base0.012.json` (the run log is in the session scratchpad; `.log` files are git-ignored)):

| tile S | window ends | first negative, odd | first negative, even | full margin at the window's end (odd / even) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| {∞} | log 2 = 0.693 | ε₁ ∈ (0.050, 0.100): +7.8×10⁻⁵ at 0.743, −6.9×10⁻² at 0.793 | ε₁ ∈ (0.100, 0.150): +7.6×10⁻⁴ at 0.793, −1.2×10⁻³ at 0.843 | 6.5×10⁻² / 1.2×10⁻³ |
| {∞, 2} | log 3 = 1.099 | ε₁ ∈ (0.015, 0.020): +1.7×10⁻⁶ at 1.1136, −8.8×10⁻⁶ at 1.1186 | ε₁ ∈ (0.040, 0.050): +3.0×10⁻⁸ at 1.1386, −1.9×10⁻⁸ at 1.1486 | 1.4×10⁻⁵ / 6×10⁻⁸ |
| {∞, 2, 3} | log 4 = 1.386 | ≲ 0.02–0.03 (−3.0×10⁻⁶ at ε = 0.020, −5.6×10⁻⁵ at 0.030; resolution-limited below) | ≲ 0.07–0.10 (−1.1×10⁻³ at ε = 0.100; resolution-limited below) | 5×10⁻¹⁰ / 8×10⁻¹³ (A420, zero side) |

*(i) The tile is tight with shrinking slack.* Each tile's positivity outlasts its window, by a slack ε₁ that falls with every prime — odd ≈ 0.07 → 0.017 → ≲ 0.02 (unresolved), even ≈ 0.12 → 0.045 → ≲ 0.1 — tracking the collapse of the full margin at the threshold (6.5×10⁻² → 1.4×10⁻⁵ → 5×10⁻¹⁰ odd) but far more slowly than it: the failing direction is not the full form's ground state. Every prime arrives before the previous tile fails, by exactly this slack. **The archimedean form alone (Connes–Consani's proven object) is positive on odd functions to δ ≈ 0.745 and on even functions to δ ≈ 0.81 — beyond the log 2 = 0.693 where it stops being the full functional, by 7% and 17%.** *Correction, lead-noticed the same day (record files corrected when noticed):* this is NOT unchecked against CC — it is CC's own Figure-6 observation, already an anchor of this program's bridge: A388 Stage A records "the Figure-6 arch-alone failure at δ ∈ (0.74, 0.76), the ODD sector first (even holds to (0.80, 0.85))", reproduced there on the corrected forms; the tile scan's brackets (odd (0.743, 0.793), even (0.793, 0.843)) reproduce that anchor a second time, on a different instrument. The lead failed to consult A388 before writing the sentence above — the same Check-4 class as A421's correction. *(ii) The odd sector fails first, and the reason is the pole's parity.* Near the window's end the missing term's sign is fixed by the edge product g(a)g(−a): for odd probes h(log q) ≈ −g(a)²·ε < 0, so the term Q_q = −C_q h is positive and dropping it lowers the form at once (S = {∞} odd at ε = 0.01: λ₁^S = 5.8×10⁻² below the full 6.2×10⁻²); for even probes h > 0, the term is negative, and the truncated even tile is briefly *more* positive than the full form (S = {∞, 2} even at ε = 0.002: 5.936×10⁻⁸ against 5.904×10⁻⁸; S = {∞} even: 1.195×10⁻³ against 1.134×10⁻³) until the minimiser finds a direction with negative autocorrelation at the missing lag (Q_q crossing to positive at ε ≈ 0.03 for S = {∞, 2}, ≈ 0.1 for S = {∞}). *(iii) The failure is the tradeoff, measured.* On every cell Q_full(c_S) > 0 — the full form is positive on the truncated form's own ground state, as it must be — and the tile fails where the missing term overtakes it: S = {∞, 2} odd, ε = 0.015 → 0.020: Q_full(c_S) 1.54×10⁻⁵ → 3.01×10⁻⁵ against Q_q 1.37×10⁻⁵ → 3.89×10⁻⁵, the edge mass rising 2.2×10⁻⁴ → 3.9×10⁻⁴ and then to 0.2 once free (ε = 0.04). The truncated minimiser buys negative autocorrelation at the missing lag with edge mass and pays for it in the full form — Q_full on the failing direction runs a factor 2–4 above the full ground state — which is why the slack is so much wider than the full margin. *(iv) What the tile says about the packing.* The p-adic balls' pairings overfill the archimedean potential the moment a prime is withheld past its lag plus the slack, and the odd sector — where the pole ladder enters with the negative sign — is the sector that overfills first: the pole term is what carries positivity (1az's "pole-carried") and the odd pole is the weaker carrier.

**The third tile re-scanned at base 0.006 (owner: "I would intuit perfect packing at the primes or zeros" — the weak power law ε₁ ∝ λ₁_full^0.17 read off the first two tiles predicts the third tile's odd slack near 0.003; tested).** Ten cells just past log 4 (odd ε ∈ {0.002, 0.004, 0.006, 0.008, 0.012}; even {0.01, 0.02, 0.03, 0.05, 0.07}), 37–47 s each. **Inconclusive, and instructive about the instrument:** the odd block sits at the pipeline's floor — λ₁^S and λ₁_full both within ±1.5×10⁻⁹ of zero at every cell, sign-indefinite (−7.6×10⁻¹⁰, −1.4×10⁻⁹, −7.1×10⁻¹⁰, +1.9×10⁻¹¹, −2.3×10⁻¹⁰), exactly the ±10⁻⁹ noise band A418's Stage 0b established at the window top — so a crossing near ε ≈ 0.003, whose true values would be of order the full margin 5×10⁻¹⁰, cannot be resolved in float64 at this a: the prediction is neither confirmed nor refuted, and the odd ε₁(S₃) stands bracketed only by the coarse scan's clear descent from ε = 0.02 (−3.0×10⁻⁶) on. The even block is worse than a floor: its values (−9.2×10⁻⁶, −3.4×10⁻⁶, −1.1×10⁻⁶, −1.1×10⁻⁵, −4.4×10⁻⁶ at base 0.006; −3.3×10⁻⁶ … −2.8×10⁻⁶ at base 0.012 on overlapping cells) vary non-monotonically in ε and in base, against the adjudicated +5.7×10⁻⁹ of the in-window cell at 1.38 (base 0.008) — the signature of 1az's near-degenerate even bottom cluster (λ₂^even ≈ 10⁻⁷ at log 4, A418) under the whitening cut, not of the form: **the even block past log 4 is unresolved at every base tested and its negatives are instrument artifacts**, which the table above already states for the "lam1_full" column and which now extends to the even ε₁(S₃) bound (retained only as "≲ 0.1" from the clear −1.1×10⁻³ at ε = 0.1). The "perfect packing at the primes" reading — the slack ε₁ → 0 as the primes accumulate, exponentially in q by the two-point law — therefore rests on two tiles; a third point needs multiprecision, not a finer base.

**Limits and honesty.** Float64 reconnaissance at base 0.012 (the A417 pipeline's coarsest base); the S = {∞, 2, 3} block past log 4 is resolution-limited: at those a the pipeline's own floor sits near 10⁻⁶ while the true full margins there are 10⁻¹²–10⁻¹⁰ (A420), so the block's `lam1_full` negatives (−9.7×10⁻⁷ at 1.391, non-monotone in ε) are quadrature artifacts of the coarse base — **not counterexamples to anything** — and its ε₁ bounds are upper bounds only; nothing here is certified; no new machinery. Checks 7/8 clean (Tate's thesis, Poisson summation, the explicit formula, finite Hermitian eigenproblems — classical; no hypothesis input; Riemann-side pure mathematics). **No RH consequence is claimed**; the tightness measured is a property of truncations, and its "every prime arrives before the previous tile fails" reading holds for the windows certified (through 1.10 odd) and is the full form's positivity beyond.

## Addendum 423 — the uncertainty principle, searched out (owner: "Search out the uncertainty principle, let the universe guide you"): measured on the prime side, it has two faces — the even sector is pole-carried with the minimiser saturating Slepian's concentration cap on the kernel's negative set to 75–96%, the odd sector is PRIME-carried past log 2 with the minimiser avoiding the well and anti-correlating at every prime lag; the archimedean part is negative on both ground states from δ ≈ 0.8

**The principle to be found.** Strip the zeros out of Weil's criterion and the statement at support δ is an inequality about Paley–Wiener functions of type a = δ/2 against an explicit kernel: (1/2π)∫|ĝ|² W_δ dr ± 2⟨χ,g⟩² ≥ 0, with W_δ = W_∞ − Σ_{log pᵏ<δ} C_{pᵏ} cos(r log pᵏ) the S(δ)-local kernel (the full form on its window; Theorem 1bj(i), 1bk(i)) and W_∞(r) = 2 Re p(−½ + ir) the cascade's potential on the critical line (A422). W_δ has a negative set N_δ — the central well [0, r₀] with W_δ(0) = ψ(¼) − log π − ΣC = −5.37 (no primes), −6.35 (prime 2), −7.62 (primes 2, 3), r₀ = 6.29 / 3.31 / 2.28, plus further negative pieces once primes enter (A417's `kernel_negative_set`: [4.82, 7.27], [9.67, 11.97], [16.25, 18.49], [27.56, 28.94], [45.15, 46.13] for the two-prime kernel). "The probe cannot resolve the well" is the principle; the question is what enforces it, and the paper's own guide is the ball: Theorem 1as's Gaussian occupant, the entropic-uncertainty saturator ("the Gaussian FAMILY saturates the entropic uncertainty bound exactly"), and 1bb's Slepian operator. Slepian's concentration theorem is the sharp form for intervals: a type-a function can place at most λ₀(a·R) of its L² mass on [−R, R], and at most the top eigenvalue of the concentration operator restricted to a union of intervals on that union — computable caps against which the minimiser can be measured.

**The instrument (`tools/research/uncertainty_anatomy.py`; results `checkpoints/uncertainty_anatomy_base0.012.json`; float64; the twoprime_recon operator with the archimedean, prime, and pole operators kept separate on one grid; 22 cells, δ = 0.30 … 1.38, both parities, 6–17 s each; the balance A + Π + P reproducing λ₁ to the printed digits on every cell and the margin curve's values — 3.336×10⁻² at 0.5 even, 7.785×10⁻² at 0.69 odd, 1.618×10⁻⁵ at 0.9 even, 1.954×10⁻⁵ at 1.09 odd — digit-for-digit).** For the full form's ground state g at each cell: the balance λ₁ = A(g) + Π(g) + P(g) (archimedean; pole; primes, the sign of each as it enters the form); the Fourier profile (1/2π)|ĝ(r)|² on [0, 80]; its mass on the central well and on the whole negative set N_δ against the two Slepian caps; the well deficit D = (1/2π)∫_{N}|ĝ|²|W_δ| and the surplus S⁺ = (1/2π)∫_{W>0}|ĝ|²W_δ; the edge mass g(a)²/‖g‖².

**Result — the even face: pole-carried, cap-saturating.** On every even cell the archimedean part is negative and the pole term cancels it to the margin: (A, Π) = (−0.346, +0.564) at δ = 0.30; (−0.866, +0.899) at 0.50; (−1.105, +1.106) at 0.69; (−1.256, +1.268) at 1.00; (−1.358, +1.392) at log 4 — with the primes a small negative correction (0 → −0.034) and λ₁ the residual, 2×10⁻¹ → 4×10⁻⁹. The even minimiser fills the negative set nearly to the concentration limit: mass on N_δ / Slepian cap on N_δ = 0.523/0.546 (96%) at 0.30, 0.748/0.784 (95%) at 0.50, 0.814/0.859 (95%) at 0.60, 0.845/0.907 (93%) at 0.69 — and, once the primes reshape N_δ, 0.649/0.715 (91%) at 0.80, 0.664/0.854 (78%) at 1.00, 0.670/0.891 (75%) at 1.09, 0.610/0.751 (81%) at 1.20, 0.615/0.853 (72%) at log 4. The deficit it incurs (0.62 → 1.66) is repaid almost entirely by the pole (0.56 → 1.39) with the positive kernel region supplying the rest (0.26 → 0.27); identically D − S⁺ = −(A + P) = Π − λ₁ on every cell. *The even uncertainty principle, as measured:* a type-a probe cannot put more than the Slepian cap of its mass into the well, and a probe that concentrates in the well has, by that very concentration, a large value at the imaginary frequency r = ∓i/2 — Π = 2|ĝ(−i/2)|² — which the pole rewards by at least the well deficit less the surplus. Both sides of the ledger are low-frequency quantities of the same function; the principle a proof needs in this sector is a lower bound on |ĝ(i/2)|² in terms of the mass a type-a function carries on [−r₀, r₀], uniform over the probes that saturate the cap. (Connes–Consani's archimedean theorem is exactly such a bound through log 2, proved by the prolate operator; the numbers here are what it has to reproduce and how it continues under the primes.)

**Result — the odd face: prime-carried, cap-avoiding.** The odd sector has no pole rescue (Π = −0.001 → −0.027, the wrong sign) and behaves oppositely: below log 2 positivity is purely archimedean (A = +0.925 at 0.30, +0.413 at 0.50, +0.090 at 0.69; the minimiser keeps only 5% → 39% of its mass in the well against caps of 55% → 91%); from δ = 0.80 on the archimedean part turns NEGATIVE (−0.031, −0.098, −0.139, −0.161, −0.187, −0.204, −0.217 at 0.80 … log 4) and **the primes carry the positivity**: P = +0.062, +0.119, +0.160, +0.183, +0.211, +0.230, +0.243 — the odd minimiser's autocorrelation is negative at every prime-power lag inside its support (the edge antisymmetry g(a)g(−a) < 0 forced on odd probes near the window's end, A422(ii), now seen as the carrier of the whole sector), so each prime term enters with a positive sign and the balance is arch against primes with the pole a −0.02 spectator; λ₁ = P − |A| − |Π| to nine decades of cancellation at log 4 (0.2431 − 0.2165 − 0.0265 = −3×10⁻⁹, the float floor). Its mass on the negative set stays at 43–48% of the 79–89% cap: the odd minimiser does not press the concentration limit; it presses the prime lags. *The odd uncertainty principle, as measured:* an odd type-a probe cannot correlate positively at the prime lags while placing its mass where the archimedean kernel is negative — the primes' positivity on the minimiser is the constraint, and a proof in this sector needs a lower bound on −Σ_{pᵏ} C_{pᵏ} h_g(log pᵏ) in terms of the mass an odd type-a function carries on N_δ. Neither face invokes a zero; both are statements about explicit kernels and Paley–Wiener functions, and both are RH on their windows.

**Against the record.** The even ledger is a re-measurement of A388 Stage B1's budget decomposition ("the even extremal balances pole (+1.08..+1.28) against dip mass (−1.25..−1.43) plus positive mass (+0.15..+0.17) — a pole-vs-well duel in an explicit 3.3-wide frequency well"): this addendum's Π = 1.11–1.30, deficit 1.14–1.45, surplus 0.15–0.16 over δ = 0.69–1.09 reproduce it; what is new on the even face is the Slepian cap and the minimiser's 75–96% saturation of it *(correction appended the same day: the lead had not consulted A388 before writing this section)*. 1az named positivity "POLE-CARRIED" from the whole-form instrument, and 1ba's three regimes (pole-carried baseband → the arch–prime draw → zero-carried) run along the reach axis τ₀ at δ = 4. The parity split on the support axis at δ ≤ log 4 — even pole-carried, odd prime-carried, the archimedean part negative on both ground states from δ ≈ 0.8 — is not in the record (no "prime-carried" anywhere in the paper); the odd sector's carrier is the new observation, and it reframes the odd certificates 1bj/1bk: what they certify is that the primes' positive contribution on odd probes exceeds the archimedean deficit at every support length through 1.10. The measured saturation of Slepian's cap by the even minimiser (96% at small δ, falling to ~75% under the primes) is the quantitative content of "the probe cannot resolve the well": it very nearly can, and the pole is what stops it.

**Limits.** Float64, base 0.012, the ground states nondegenerate on every cell (λ₂/λ₁ ≥ 10² even, ≥ 10³ odd, so the balance decompositions are direction-stable, unlike 1az's δ = 4 cluster); the Fourier profile integrated to r = 80 (mass beyond it ≤ 1% at every cell); the caps by Nyström at 60 nodes per piece; the log 4 odd cell at the float floor (−3×10⁻⁹) is the pipeline's noise, not a sign. No RH consequence claimed; nothing certified. Checks 7/8 clean (Slepian, Paley–Wiener, the explicit formula, Hermitian eigenproblems — classical; no hypothesis input; the "universe" consulted is Theorem 1as's ball and its entropic saturator, pure mathematics).

## Addendum 425 — the mechanism proof over the one-prime window (owner: "Do the mechanism proof over the one-prime window"): Weil's full functional is positive on [0, 1.09375] in BOTH sectors, proved uniformly over every probe by Slepian concentration and a 31-prolate head matrix — no Temple trial, no Birman–Schwinger count, no zero; the even sector's certified top moves from 1.0 (Theorem 1bj) to 1.09375, by mechanism

**The bound (the uncertainty principle of A423, made a proof).** For a real probe g on [−a, a] of fixed parity, ĝ its Fourier transform (exponential type a), the one-prime form Q(g) = (1/2π)∫|ĝ|²W dr ± 2⟨χ,g⟩², W = W_∞ − C₂cos(r log 2), is the full functional at every support length below log 3 (Theorem 1bj(i); below log 2 the prime term vanishes on the autocorrelation, so it is the full form there as well). Fix Ω and let W_out = W_∞(Ω) − C₂; since W_∞(r) = Re ψ(¼ + ir/2) − log π is increasing in r > 0 (d/dr Re ψ = −½ Im ψ′(¼ + ir/2) = ½ Σ_k r(¼+k)/|¼+k+ir/2|⁴ > 0) *(the factor ½ restored at round 286's observation; sign and positivity unaffected)*, W ≥ W_out on |r| ≥ Ω. Hence for EVERY g: **Q(g) ≥ ⟨g, M g⟩ with M = A_in + W_out(I − K) ± 2χχᵀ**, A_in the band form (1/2π)∫_{|r|≤Ω}|ĝ|²W and K the Slepian concentration operator of (a, Ω) on L²[−a, a] (0 ≤ K ≤ I, eigenfunctions the prolate spheroidal wave functions ψ_k, eigenvalues λ_k decreasing). In the prolate basis K is diagonal, A_in couples ψ_j to ψ_k by at most M_W√(λ_jλ_k) (Cauchy–Schwarz on the band, M_W = max|W| there), and the pole is rank one; so with a head (k ≤ NH) and the tail (its orthogonal complement in L²[−a,a]): the tail block is ≥ q_⊥ = W_out(1 − Λ_tail) − M_W Λ_tail − [odd] 2‖P_⊥χ‖², the coupling is ≤ b = (M_W + W_out)√Λ_tail + 2‖χ‖‖P_⊥χ‖, Λ_tail = sup_{f ⊥ head}⟨f,Kf⟩, and **λ_min(Q) ≥ λ_min([[λ_min(M_head), −b], [−b, q_⊥]])**. The uncertainty principle is the tail: a probe orthogonal to the first NH+1 prolates has at most Λ_tail of its mass on the band, where the kernel is negative, and the rest where the kernel exceeds W_out > 0. Positivity of the whole infinite-dimensional form collapses to a finite matrix plus that inequality.

**Stage 0 (`mechanism_stage0.py`, float64).** The bound is positive at every cell of the one-prime window in both sectors, at Ω = 40 and 80, capturing 60–88% of the margin curve's λ₁ (Ω = 80: even 0.8: 1.59×10⁻⁴ vs 1.81×10⁻⁴; even 1.0: 7.96×10⁻⁷ vs 9.41×10⁻⁷; even 1.09: 5.59×10⁻⁸ vs 7.9×10⁻⁸; odd 1.095: 1.38×10⁻⁵), the first tail prolate's concentration 10⁻³²–10⁻³⁵, the coupling ≤ 10⁻⁷. Feasible; the two closed-form identities the rigorous version rests on were checked to 12 digits (λ_k = (c/2π)|μ_k|² with μ_k from the finite-Fourier eigen-relation at x = 0; the pole vector by ∫P_n(x)e^{sx}dx = 2i_n(s)).

**Stage 1 (`oneprime_slepian_certificate.py`; every quantity an enclosure).** The cell a = 35/64 (δ = 1.09375 < log 3 = 1.0986), Ω = 64, so c = aΩ = 35 EXACTLY; NH = 30 (31 prolates per parity; Shannon number 2c/π = 22.3); Legendre truncation n < 240; Simpson pitch h = 10⁻⁴ (10⁴ cells on [0, 1]). The chain: (1) *verified prolates* — the tridiagonal of Slepian's commuting operator L = −d/dx(1−x²)d/dx + c²x² in the normalized-Legendre basis (interval entries, exact in c² = 1225), float eigenpairs, a rigorous residual r_k = ‖(L − χ_k)v_k‖ per head vector (padded with zeros, the coupling beyond the truncation included; max 2.4×10⁻¹¹), a rigorous Sturm count on the interval tridiagonal with the last pivot widened by the Schur bound for the strictly diagonally dominant infinite tail, certifying exactly one true eigenvalue in each bracket and none between (min gap 66.6), hence ‖ψ_k − φ_k‖ ≤ ε_k = √2 r_k/gap_k + normalisation slack (max 2.8×10⁻¹³) with φ_k the float vector as stored — an explicit polynomial, the head basis; (2) *Slepian eigenvalues* λ_k = (c/2π)|μ_k|² with ε_k propagated, resolvable through k* = 22 (λ ≈ 7×10⁻²⁵ even, 1.2×10⁻²³ odd) and beyond by monotonicity; (3) *the head matrix in the explicit basis*: the exact Gram Γ = β_j·β_k (‖Γ − I‖ ≤ 1.3×10⁻¹³); the band form A_in(j,k) = (aΩμ_jμ̄_k/2π)∫_{−1}^{1}φ_jφ_kW(Ωx)dx plus the eigen-relation's residual slop ((√(2π/c) + |μ|)ε per vector, Cauchy–Schwarz); the concentration Gram likewise; the pole vector by the modified-spherical-Bessel closed form (interval series with a geometric tail); the band integral by Simpson with the rigorous error (h⁵/2880)·sup|f⁗| assembled from per-cell sups of |φ^{(l)}| (node values by floating-point Clenshaw with a rigorous running error bound — every rounding an additive coefficient perturbation η_k, |Σ η_kP_k| ≤ Σ|η_k| — plus a Lipschitz step whose top order is Markov's endpoint bound Σ|c_n|P_n^{(l)}(1)) and per-cell kernel majorants |W^{(m)}| ≤ (m!/2^m)Σ_k|¼+k+ir/2|^{−(m+1)} + C₂log^m2 (first 40 terms + integral tail); the kernel at the 2×10⁴ nodes by a **Stirling enclosure** new to the arc: after the core's shift to Re z ≥ 25, Binet's second formula ψ(z) = ln z − 1/(2z) − 2∫t/((t²+z²)(e^{2πt}−1))dt with 1/(t²+z²) expanded to ten terms gives the Stirling series exactly and the remainder |R| ≤ 2|B₂₂|/44/(|z|²⁰ d_z), d_z = min_t|t²+z²| ≥ min(|z|², 2xy) — width 10⁻¹³ against the committed Binet-grid enclosure's 7×10⁻⁷, contained in it at every check node (the instrument asserts containment on 21 nodes); **THEOREM (the mechanism proof).** Even sector: λ_min(M_head) ≥ 4.32329×10⁻⁸ (float 4.34201×10⁻⁸), final λ_min(Q) ≥ **4.3231×10⁻⁸**; odd sector: λ_min(M_head) ≥ 1.356648×10⁻⁵ (float 1.356688×10⁻⁵), final λ_min(Q) ≥ **1.3566×10⁻⁵** (the certified head eigenvalue ranges χ ∈ [34.2, 4531] / [103.2, 4656], the Sturm tail-widening computed against the actual range). **The one-prime semi-local Weil form — Weil's full functional below log 3 — is positive for every probe of support length 1.09375 in the even sector (λ_min ≥ 4.3231×10⁻⁸) and in the odd sector (λ_min ≥ 1.3566×10⁻⁵), hence, by domain nesting, positive on [0, 1.09375] in both sectors.** What is new against Theorem 1bj: the even sector's certified top was 1.0 (the pole-inclusive count's cell), now 1.09375 — the whole one-prime window to within 0.005 of log 3 in both sectors — and the *method*: no Temple trial, no Birman–Schwinger count, no spectral-gap premise; the infinite-dimensional problem is closed by Slepian's concentration theorem and a 31×31 verified matrix. Checks 7/8 clean (Slepian, Paley–Wiener, Binet, Stirling, IEEE-754 — classical; no hypothesis input). **No RH consequence is claimed.**
