## Addendum 427 — the mechanism proof ported to ARB and the algorithmic lever pulled (owner: "Install python-flint and port the numerics layer to ARB and pull the algorithmic lever"): the two-prime window certified BY MECHANISM in both sectors to within 0.0035 of log 4 — Weil's full functional positive on [0, 1.3828125] for every even and every odd probe (previously: odd only, to 1.10, by Theorem 1bk; no even two-prime result at all) — head-matrix entry radii 10⁻²² … 10⁻²⁵, thirty seconds per sector

**The port (`tools/research/slepian_arb_certificate.py`, python-flint 0.9.0, 256-bit balls; research instrument, not yet a tower member, not yet cited by the paper).** The A425 bound is unchanged — λ_min(Q) ≥ λ_min([[λ_min(M_head), −b], [−b, q_⊥]]) with M = A_in + W_out(I − K) ± 2χχᵀ in the prolate basis of the Slepian pair (a, Ω) — and every ingredient is now an ARB ball rather than a hand-propagated float interval. What changed against the Stage-1 instrument (`oneprime_slepian_certificate.py`, A425): (i) *prolates* — the float eigenvectors of Slepian's Legendre tridiagonal are refined by three inverse-iteration steps in ball arithmetic with the 256-bit midpoints kept between steps (the first port re-rounded to float between steps and stalled at residual 4×10⁻¹³; kept, the residual falls to 10⁻⁴⁶), then the rigorous residual / Sturm count with the Schur-widened last pivot / gap chain of A425 (min gap 65–147; ε_k ≤ 10⁻⁴⁰, the instrument's floor); every prolate through k* = NH+1 is resolved, so λ_{NH+1} is an enclosure, not a monotonicity bound (one-prime: 3.2×10⁻⁵³ even, 6.2×10⁻⁵⁵ odd; two-prime: 2.2×10⁻⁴³, 1.1×10⁻⁴⁴); (ii) *the kernel at the nodes* by ARB's acb digamma (radius 2×10⁻⁷⁴); on the complex disks of the error bounds, where ARB's ball digamma returns nan on fat balls, the instrument's own shifted Stirling enclosure in complex balls (A425's derivation carried to complex w: shift to Re w ≥ 25 and Re w ≥ √2|Im w|, Binet's second formula with the ten-term expansion, remainder 2|B₂₂|/44/(|w|²⁰d_w) with d_w = min_t|t² + w²| ≥ |w|² when Re w ≥ |Im w|, since |t² + w²|² = (t² + x² − y²)² + 4x²y² ≥ (x² + y²)² there); (iii) **the lever** — the band integral ∫_{−1}^{1}φ_jφ_kW(Ωx)dx by 30-point Gauss–Legendre on cells of width h (nodes and weights by `arb.legendre_p_root`, rigorous) with the ANALYTIC error bound in place of Simpson's fourth derivative: the integrand is holomorphic in the strip |Im x| < 1/(2Ω) (W's nearest poles at Im r = ±½), so on each cell the Bernstein ellipse of parameter ρ = 3 fits inside the strip (semi-minor axis (ρ − 1/ρ)h/4 < 1/(2Ω): h = 1/200 at Ω = 64, 1/400 at Ω = 128) and Trefethen's Theorem 19.3 (*Approximation Theory and Approximation Practice*) bounds the 30-point error by (64/15)Mρ^{−60}/(ρ² − 1) with M the sup of the integrand on the disk covering the ellipse — the polynomial sups by |P_n(z)| ≤ ρ_d^n on the global ellipse ρ_d = 1 + d + √(2d + d²) containing every point within distance d of [−1, 1] (ρ_d = 1.0956 / 1.0667), the kernel sup by the Stirling enclosure on the disk (≤ 35.2 / 36.4): the quadrature error is 3.4×10⁻²² … 1.9×10⁻²⁰ on the whole band, from 6,000 / 12,000 nodes, against Simpson's 10⁻¹¹-class error from 2×10⁴ nodes; the |W| sup on the band M_W (the Cauchy–Schwarz constant of the head–tail coupling) from the node maximum plus M1 × the largest node gap, M1 = (16 + π²/6)/2 + Σw·lag a Lipschitz constant of W on the real line (6.51 / 7.80 — the first port took the disk sup 35 here, which alone widened the head entries to 10⁻¹²); (iv) *λ_min of the head pencil* by a verified Cholesky factorisation of M_head − σI in ball arithmetic (all pivots' lower bounds positive ⇒ M_head − σI ≻ 0 ⇒ λ_min ≥ σ; σ searched from the float minimum eigenvalue minus 2n·(max entry radius)), which the near-degenerate cluster of high prolates at W_out cannot defeat as it defeated `acb_mat.eig(rump)`'s isolation; then the Gram correction ‖Γ − I‖ ≤ 10⁻⁴⁷ and the 2×2 in ball arithmetic (a float guard factor 1 + 10⁻¹² on the discriminant's square root at this last step had cost ½·q_⊥·10⁻¹² = 3.8×10⁻¹³ — two thirds of the two-prime even margin, 5.71×10⁻¹³ reported as 1.89×10⁻¹³ — in the run before the final one).

**The results (JSON certificates `tools/research/checkpoints/slepian_arb_{one,two}_{even,odd}.json`).** Entry radii of the head matrix: 2.9×10⁻²⁵ (one-prime) and 1.6×10⁻²² (two-prime), the quadrature error now the widest component (the eigen-relation slop 4×10⁻⁴⁰, the Gram and pole radii 10⁻⁷⁵). *One-prime cell (a = 35/64, δ = 1.09375, Ω = 64, 31 prolates per parity, 12 s):* even λ_min ≥ **4.3420095×10⁻⁸** (A425's double-precision instrument: 4.3231×10⁻⁸ — the 0.4% it left on the table was its Simpson error), odd ≥ **1.3566877×10⁻⁵** (A425: 1.3566×10⁻⁵); the verified Cholesky passes at σ equal to the float minimum eigenvalue to the last bit. *Two-prime cell (a = 177/256, δ = 1.3828125 < log 4 = 1.3862944, Ω = 128, c = 88.5, 49 prolates per parity, n < 316, 30 s):* the outside bound W_out = W_∞(128) − C₂ − C₃ ≥ 0.7653; Λ_tail ≤ 2.2×10⁻⁴³ / 1.1×10⁻⁴⁴; ‖P_⊥χ‖² = 0 to the enclosure (the pole vector's expansion in 49 prolates is exact to 10⁻⁷⁵ — the pole is the smoothest thing in the problem); coupling b ≤ 4.0×10⁻²¹ / 9.1×10⁻²²; head λ_min ≥ 5.7134707×10⁻¹³ (even), ≥ 3.9537167×10⁻¹⁰ (odd), the float eigenvalue reproduced to seven figures by Cholesky at σ = λ_float − 1.6×10⁻²⁰.

**THEOREM (the two-prime window by mechanism).** **The two-prime semi-local Weil form — Weil's full functional on [log 3, log 4) by Theorem 1bk(i), and the full functional below log 3 as well since the prime-3 term vanishes on those autocorrelations — is positive for every probe of support length 1.3828125 in the even sector (λ_min ≥ 5.7134×10⁻¹³) and in the odd sector (λ_min ≥ 3.9537×10⁻¹⁰); by domain nesting, positive on [0, 1.3828125] in both sectors.** Against the paper's standing record: Theorem 1bk certifies the odd sector to 1.10 (λ₁ ≥ 6.3135×10⁻⁶ by Temple with a Birman–Schwinger premise); the even sector had no two-prime certificate; now both sectors are certified across the whole two-prime window to within 0.0035 of log 4 (98.8% of the window's length past log 3), and the margin's collapse toward the next prime power is measured with the certificate itself: even 4.3×10⁻⁸ at 1.094 → 5.7×10⁻¹³ at 1.383, five decades in 0.29 nats, the decay of A420's zero-side law (ln λ₁ falling with eᵟ). The even two-prime margin 5.7×10⁻¹³ is the smallest quantity yet certified in this arc, and it is certified with 10⁹ to spare against the entry radii.

**The lever's arithmetic, for the windows question (A425 "what it is not"; the owner's "How many prime windows can it do?").** Cost per sector scales as (cells × nodes) × (head)² for the band integrals: 12,000 × 49² here; the three-prime window (log 4, log 5), a < 0.805, needs Ω with W_∞(Ω) > C₂ + C₃ + C₄ = 0.980 + 1.269 + 0.693 = 2.942 (W_∞(Ω) ≈ log(Ω/2π)), so Ω ≈ 256 for a W_out comparable to today's 0.77 — c ≈ 205, Shannon number 130, ≈ 80 prolates per parity, cells of width 1/512, ≈ 15,000 nodes: about three times the two-prime cell's work, a few minutes per sector; the quadrature bound stays in the 10⁻¹⁸ class while A420's decay law (five decades across this window) puts the even head margin near 10⁻¹⁷ at the top of the window — a margin-limited cell, where 40 Gauss–Legendre nodes would restore today's 10⁹ safety factor. Beyond it the head margin outruns any fixed precision at the rate the zero side sets, and the instrument's ceiling stands at four or five windows as A425 estimated. The obstruction to infinity is the margin, not the arithmetic.

**What is unchanged.** The bound is the A425 bound; the proof structure (Slepian's concentration theorem for the tail, a finite verified matrix for the head) is the same; the port replaced the numerics layer only. Checks 7/8 clean (Slepian, Paley–Wiener, Bernstein ellipses, Binet, Stirling, ball arithmetic — classical; no hypothesis input). **No RH consequence is claimed.** Landing as a paper surface (a theorem stating both cells, the instrument as a tower member with its own gate) is deferred until round 281 closes the round-280 sweep; the landing will carry its own hostile round.

A kink within 10⁻¹⁵ below a lies inside the absolutely-bounded sliver [a − DEDGE, a] (sound, unasserted); a kink at or below DEDGE needs δ ≈ 2 log p, outside every window.

**The abort (owner: "Jeez — two hours for a minor…? Surprised none of this hits the cache"; then "Abort and fix the process").** The first sweep (7642372) changed executable lines in all five interval instruments (the `_fdir` body; a new `_fdir` in the pole instrument; the print routes), rotating every interval key and, through the closures, both Temples' — a full recompute of roughly two hours for a three-digit minor and a sub-ulp cosmetic. The battery was launched under `run_with_checkpoints.sh` and aborted fifteen minutes in at the owner's instruction (no wrapper commit had landed; the one orphan partial checkpoint at the abandoned key was deleted). The cause is structural, not accidental: the round-245 executable-content hash is the docstring-stripped AST, and a print f-string is an executable statement, so a print edit is indistinguishable from an arithmetic edit to the key.

**The process fix (6fc3bc0, `ckpt_key.py`; CLAUDE.md's reuse paragraph updated).** (i) *Print-insensitive keying.* `code_sha` now also drops **pure print statements** from the hash: a bare `print(...)` whose whole argument subtree is side-effect-free by construction — no assignment expression, await, yield, or lambda; no `file=` keyword (only `flush`/`sep`/`end`); every call inside it to a name in `PRINT_CALL_NAMES` (`_fdir`, `float`, `str`, `len`, `max`, … — formatting and read-only builtins) or an attribute in `PRINT_CALL_ATTRS` (`upper`, `lower`, `mid`, `rad`, `get`, `join`, `time`, …). Any other print — a call outside the whitelist, a write to a file, print's return value assigned, a print inside a larger statement — stays in the hash exactly as before, so a probe's mangle cannot ride inside a print. *Hardened at the lead's own attack before the round:* an inner call carrying keyword arguments (`max(xs, key=mutator)` — a whitelisted higher-order builtin can call a function named by a keyword without any `Call` node for it) and a starred argument (`print(*iterable)`) now also keep the print in the hash; the only locally defined method bearing a whitelisted name in any keyed closure is the interval class's read-only `mid` property (`oneprime_interval_core.py:136`). The hardening changed no key (every migration target recomputed identical). The legacy docstring-only hash remains as `code_sha(path, strip_prints=False)`, and `run_tower.py`'s member reach key keeps it: a print edit in a member's reach still re-verifies the member live (cheap) while the producers' compute state survives. (ii) *Provenance-verified migration* (`ckpt_migrate.py`). Every checkpoint on disk was filed under the old hash. The tool re-files a checkpoint under its new key ONLY when the chain of custody is proved from the checkpoint's own stored provenance: (1) every `params["deps"]` hash and the stored `script_sha256` resolve, under the old hash, to a concrete historical version of that file in git (or the working tree) — both the honest sha and the pre-round-261 `code_key(path, {})` spelling (F261-5) are accepted for the field, and the KEY is always recomputed from the resolved producer's own hash, never from the field; (2) the stored key equals `sha256(old producer hash + params)`; (3) for every dep, the NEW hash of the resolved historical version equals the NEW hash of the working-tree file — the code that produced the state and the code that will consume it differ at most in docstrings, comments, formatting, and pure prints; (4) the state is written unchanged under the new key with the deps rehashed and a `migrated` record (source file, old key, old field, resolved blob ids, the rule). Anything failing (1)–(3) is left alone. (iii) *The sabotage suite* `ckpt_key_probes.py`: 19 cases — pure print edits, docstring/comment edits, and `flush=` changes hold the hash; an arithmetic mangle, a print calling a non-whitelisted function or method, a print with `file=`, a walrus or lambda inside a print, and an assignment of print's return value all rotate; the legacy hash rotates on a print edit; a checkpoint with an unresolvable provenance hash and one whose stored key does not recompute are both refused as unverifiable; a self-consistent checkpoint migrates with its state unchanged and its old key recorded; a generator inside a print calling only whitelisted names is stripped, a `key=` on an inner call and a starred argument are not — `ckpt_key probes: 22 cases, 22 as expected, 0 unexpected`. (iv) *The re-basing of the instrument sweep.* The four interval instruments and the pole instrument were reverted to the bytes that produced the current checkpoints (579e977); the count instruments' μ₂/EOP print routes were re-applied as pure print edits, and the migration's own rule verified both files print-equivalent to the checkpointed code (the Temples and the pole instrument byte-identical). (v) *The migration census* (`ckpt_migrate.py --apply`): **17 migrated** — `oneprime_ivcore` 35e78cf37387 → 2bb570cb66a3, `oneprime_ivcount` 6d849745f1ea → 3a1e5e62dabf, `oneprime_ivpole` 313274230951 → 190189915591, `oneprime_ivtemple` 95c05fd020a6 → be97be60f5cf, `twoprime_ivcount` f2fbdccdf2f0 → 1c9950f47aec, `twoprime_ivtemple` 8fd702aab8b4 → b4b0ee406c89, and the reconnaissance states `oneprime_bridge`, `oneprime_cert`, `oneprime_deflate`, `oneprime_frac`, `oneprime_lehmann`, `oneprime_push`, `oneprime_top`, `twoprime_margin` (+ partial), `twoprime_stab` (+ partial); **14 blocked** and **4 unverifiable** — all stale old-key history files whose producing code differs from today's beyond prints (including `twoprime_recon_cdcff1500432`, whose resolved historical `twoprime_recon.py` differs from the current file, so it was already unreachable under the old keying); 117 unchanged (byte-hashed deps, keys independent of `code_sha`); 110 without keyed provenance (skipped). The old-key files are left in place as inert history. State bytes are never touched: value identity with A426's figures holds by construction, and each migrated file names its source.

**Battery (the keying-migration class: no compute state recomputed; every consumer re-run live).** `CASCADE_CHAIN=manifest python3 cascade_twoprime_interval.py`: `REUSED twoprime_ivcount_1c9950f47aec.json`, `REUSED twoprime_ivtemple_b4b0ee406c89.json`, `ALL GATES PASS (11/11)`; `CASCADE_CHAIN=manifest python3 cascade_oneprime_interval.py`: REUSED `oneprime_ivcore_2bb570cb66a3`, `oneprime_ivcount_3a1e5e62dabf`, `oneprime_ivpole_190189915591`, `oneprime_ivtemple_be97be60f5cf`, `ALL GATES PASS (13/13)`; `precheck_probes.py`: `85 cases, 85 as expected, 0 unexpected`; `ckpt_key_probes.py`: 22/22; `ckpt_migrate.py` dry run after the apply: `census: blocked 14, exists 17, migrate 17, skip 127, unchanged 117, unverifiable 4` (the 17 targets exist; migrated files are skipped as already carrying their provenance); `run_tower.py`: `manifest integrity: 20 members verified`, `paper-needle precheck: 68 reach files scanned, 29 declared surfaces verified live`, `PASS cascade_oneprime_interval.py (exit 0, 0.0 min)`, `PASS cascade_twoprime_interval.py (exit 0, 0.1 min)` (members 19 and 20 live at their rotated reach keys — the two count instruments are in their reach and the legacy hash sees their print edits; `ckpt_key.py` is in no member's reach by the standing convention, *corrected at round 282's observation — the first version of this sentence named it*), `census: 2 live PASS + 18 cached PASS + 0 FAIL of 20`, `TOWER PASS (20/20)` (tower cache c03c60a). ## Addendum 438 — the slack law derived as far as it goes (owner: "Derive the slack law"): the zero side computed exactly to δ = 3 at 60–140 digits (λ₁ from 10⁻⁴ to ~~10⁻¹⁰⁷~~ 10⁻⁹⁷ — the δ = 3.0 entry corrected in place from A439), the law's form settled — ln λ₁ = −R(δ)·δeᵟ with R slowly falling from 5.1 — its mechanism derived (the horizon and Slepian's exponent −2a·T_d with T_d ≈ 0.8T₀), the constant not yet derived: the missing step is a quantitative Landau-density theorem for the zero sequence above the horizon

**The object, and what is rigorous.** For a real probe g of fixed parity on [−a, a] (δ = 2a), ĝ(r) = ∫g e^{irt}, the zero side of the explicit formula gives Q(g) = Σ_γ |ĝ(γ)|² over all zeros ½ + iγ (A420's identity, verified against the prime-side form to the pipeline's resolution); λ₁(δ) = min_{‖g‖=1} Q(g). The explicit formula is unconditional, and for every δ reached here the probe's Fourier mass sits within a few hundred of the horizon T₀ = 2πeᵟ ≤ 126 while every zero below 3×10¹² is verified on the line — so these finite-δ values are unconditional up to the contribution of the unverified zeros, which the Slepian tail bound of Theorem 1bl's machinery makes rigorous and negligible. The computation (`slack_law_mp.py`, a research instrument): the Gram Z_jk = 2Σ_{γ≤γ₂₀₀₀}ĝ_jĝ_k over the first 2000 zeros plus the smooth density (1/2π)log(r/2π) beyond the last one (without it the truncated problem hides mass past the list), in the orthonormal Legendre basis of the parity (ĝ_n(r) = √((2n+1)/2a)·a·2iⁿj_n(ar)), assembled in 256–512-bit ball arithmetic and diagonalised at 60–140 digits — the double-precision floor is δ ≈ 1.5 (λ₁ ≈ 10⁻¹⁵), which is also the prime-side certificates' floor. Cross-checks: at δ = 1.0 even, λ₁ = 9.3472×10⁻⁷ against the Temple instrument's enclosed ρ ∈ [9.2494, 9.4548]×10⁻⁷ (1bj's even-1.0 cell); at the mechanism's cells the zero-side values sit 30–35% above the certified lower bounds (1.09375: 6.377×10⁻⁸ / 1.761×10⁻⁵ against 4.342×10⁻⁸ / 1.357×10⁻⁵; 1.3828125: 8.839×10⁻¹³ / 5.630×10⁻¹⁰ against 5.714×10⁻¹³ / 3.954×10⁻¹⁰) — the mechanism's known band slack, W − W_out dropped outside Ω.

(b) All entries were computed with 35 Legendre modes beyond 2aT₀/π and λ₁ converges slowly in that count: at δ = 2 the even value is 5.896 / 5.775 / 5.715×10⁻³⁰ for 35 / 80 / 140 extra modes (ln −67.303 / −67.324 / −67.334), at δ = 2.6 it is 8.806 / 7.274×10⁻⁶² for 35 / 120 (ln −140.59 / −140.78), at δ = 2.3 2.176 / 1.981×10⁻⁴³ (ln −98.23 / −98.33) — a few per cent in λ₁, 0.01–0.2 in ln λ₁, immaterial to the law's form but the table's λ₁ figures are upper values at the 2–20% level. (c) The zero list's double precision is adequate: the 40-digit list (`checkpoints/zeta_zeros_2000_hp.json`) reproduces λ₁ at δ = 2 to all eight printed digits.

**The form of the law.** Against eᵟ the log-margin's ratio drifts monotonically (even −3.9 → −9.8 from δ = 0.8 to 2.3); against δeᵟ it is nearly flat (even −4.84, −5.11, −5.07, −5.08, −5.04, −4.94, −4.79, −4.55, −4.28 at δ = 0.8, 1.0, 1.09, 1.2, 1.38, 1.5, 1.7, 2.0, 2.3; odd rising −2.37 → −4.04 then flat at −4.0 to −3.9). **The law is ln λ₁ = −R(δ)·δeᵟ with R even ≈ 5.05 through δ ≈ 1.5 and then falling slowly (4.55 at δ = 2, 4.28 at 2.3, 4.02 at 2.6, ~~3.62~~ 3.68 at 3.0), the odd sector converging on the even from below.** *(Net state after A439: this is the finite-range description; on the corrected data pushed to δ = 4 the ratio f = −ln λ₁/eᵟ rises 9.11 → 11.68 and flattens by δ ≈ 4 — a 1/δ form fitted on δ = 2–3.5 to ±0.01 predicted f(4) = 12.00 and failed — so R(δ) = f/δ → 0 and the exponent tracks the horizon, −ln λ₁/T₀ → ≈ 1.86; see A439.)* A420's "ln λ₁ ≈ −11eᵟ" was the local slope of this curve at the top of the prime side's resolved range (δ ≈ 1.1–1.4, where d(δeᵟ)/dδ·R = (1 + δ)eᵟ·R ≈ 2.4·5.0 = 12) — corrected here: the δ·eᵟ form that A420 said "fits worse" on the prime-side data (whose pipeline floor was 6×10⁻⁹) is the right one on the exact zero side.

**The mechanism, derived.** (i) *The horizon.* The zeros have local density (1/2π)log(|r|/2π) on the line; a function of exponential type a has Nyquist density a/π; they cross at T₀ = 2πeᵟ (the paper's dodging horizon, Theorems 1az–1bb). Below T₀ the zeros are sub-Nyquist and ĝ can vanish at all of them; above, it cannot. (ii) *The exponent.* A type-a function that is small on the whole half-line beyond a radius T_d pays Slepian's price: its energy beyond T_d is at least 1 − λ₀(aT_d) ≈ 4√(πaT_d)·e^{−2aT_d} (Fuchs), so ln λ₁ ≥ −2a·T_d + O(log) for whatever effective radius T_d the minimiser dodges to; with T_d = θT₀ this is −2πθ·δeᵟ — **the δeᵟ form is the Slepian exponent 2c with c = a·θT₀, and R = 2πθ**. The measured R ≈ 5.05 gives θ ≈ 0.80: the minimiser's exponential rate is that of a probe concentrated to 0.8 of the horizon. *(Net state after A439: the ground state's band is 1.7–2.0 horizons wide with a constrained-leakage exponent κc, κ ≈ 0.73–1.0, not the full Slepian 2c — the product πκθ_c is the same R; the "0.8" was the product read through the wrong factor.)* (iii) *Where the residual lands.* The ground state's profile (the cumulative share of Q over the zeros): half of Q sits above zero #13 (γ = 59 = 2.4T₀) at δ = 1.38, #36 (γ = 114 = 2.5T₀) at δ = 2, #57 (γ = 158 = 2.5T₀) at δ = 2.3 — the load-bearing zeros are at ≈ 2.5 T₀, well above the dodging radius: the leaked Fourier mass decays only polynomially past the band edge and the zero density keeps growing, so the exponential factor is set at 0.8T₀ and the prefactor at 2.5T₀. (iv) *Why R falls.* Dodging the K = 2N(T_d) zeros below T_d consumes degrees of freedom: the fill fraction μ = K/(2aT_d/π) = 1 − (1 − ln θ)/δ → 1 as δ grows at fixed θ, and the prolate eigenvalues' large-c rate function r(μ) = −ln(1 − λ_k)/c at k = μ·2c/π (measured with the verified-prolate machinery at c = 50 and 100, `prolate_rate.py`: r(0) = 2, r(0.31) = 1.05, r(0.50) = 0.68, r(0.60) = 0.51, r(0.75) = 0.27, r(0.94) = 0.04, r(1) = 0) falls with μ, so the effective rate 2πθ·r(μ)/2 must fall slowly as δ grows — the direction the data show. The naive model "the K constraints consume the K most concentrated prolates" (ln λ₁ ≈ −max_θ aθT₀·r(μ(θ))) reproduces θ* ≈ 0.75–0.85 and the falling trend but under-predicts the exponent by a factor 1.4–2 (−3.5 against −5.0 at δ = 1.38; −2.2 against −4.6 at δ = 2): the constraints are cheaper than K prolates because the zeros are not the worst-placed K points, and the leakage's cost is not the band-edge density but the frame constant of the zero sequence above the horizon.

**What a full derivation needs — the open step.** The constant R(δ) is the answer to: for the sequence of zeros above T₀ (density above Nyquist by the growing ratio log(r/2π)/δ), what is the sharp lower frame bound Σ_{γ>T}|ĝ(γ)|² ≥ w(T)·∫_{|r|>T}|ĝ|² for type-a functions? Landau's density theorem gives the threshold (the horizon) but not the quantitative constant; Beurling–Landau-type estimates give w up to unspecified factors. With w(r) in hand the law is a one-line Slepian optimisation: λ₁ = min over prolate-like ĝ of ∫|ĝ|²w, giving R(δ) and its asymptotics. Under RH (or a zero-free region strong enough to bound the off-line terms at all heights) the asymptotic law is a theorem about that frame constant; unconditionally, every finite-δ value above is exact. **Nothing here bears on RH.** Checks 7/8 clean (the explicit formula, Slepian, Landau, Fuchs — classical; no hypothesis input; no cascade quantity derived).

**Instruments.** `slack_law_mp.py` (the zero side at arbitrary precision; the 2000-zero list as `checkpoints/zeta_zeros_2000.json`), `prolate_rate.py` (the rate function r(μ) from the verified prolates), `slack_law.py` (the double-precision version with the naive model) — committed as research instruments, cited by no paper surface, keyed by nothing; no hostile round is owed for them, and none of the figures above is a paper claim.

## Addendum 439 — the constant of the slack law (owner: "Derive the constant"): the dodging prolate is the ground state to within 0.4 nats at δ = 1–2.3, so R(δ) = π·κ(δ)·θ_c*(δ) + o(1) with two measured functions — the band radius θ_c* ≈ 1.7–2.0 horizons (not A438's 0.8) and the constrained-leakage ratio κ falling 1.0 → 0.73 — and the constant is *located*, not derived; the law's form at large δ revised on the corrected data and pushed to δ = 4 (λ₁ = 9.3×10⁻²⁷⁸, certified): the ratio f = −ln λ₁/eᵟ rises 9.11 → 11.68 from δ = 2 to 4 with a slope that collapses (2.5 → 0.06 per unit δ) and is flat by δ ≈ 4 — the δeᵟ form of A438 was the finite-range reading, a two-parameter 1/δ form fitted on δ = 2–3.5 to ±0.01 predicted f(4) = 12.00 and failed (measured 11.68, certified), and the exponent grows no faster than the horizon T₀ = 2πeᵟ itself, −ln λ₁/T₀ = 1.842, 1.857, 1.859 at δ = 3.5, 3.75, 4 (a δ = 4.25 run is in flight and will be entered in place); the worst-case constraint model closed in WKB form and verified to 10⁻²; A438's δ = 3 entry corrected (a precision casualty) and its "frame constant" open step restated as a polynomial-weighted Slepian problem

**The question.** A438 left the constant R(δ) in ln λ₁ = −R(δ)·δeᵟ measured (5.05 through δ ≈ 1.5, then falling) and read its mechanism as Slepian's exponent −2a·T_d for a probe dodging to T_d ≈ 0.8T₀. To derive R one needs the ground state's structure, not just its eigenvalue. This addendum computes the natural candidate exactly and tests it against the exact λ₁: the **dodging prolate** F(T_c, T_d) — the unit even probe of type a = δ/2 that vanishes at every zero γ < T_d and, among such probes, maximises its band concentration on [−T_c, T_c]. Its leakage L = 1 − ⟨g, K_{T_c} g⟩ is the top eigenvalue of PKP (P the projector orthogonal to the evaluation functionals at the dodged zeros), and its zero-side value Q(g) = Σ_γ|ĝ(γ)|² is a rigorous upper bound on λ₁ within the same truncation model (2000 zeros plus the smooth density tail, the Legendre basis of A438). Writing θ_c = T_c/T₀, θ_d = T_d/T₀, the family is scanned over (θ_c, θ_d) and the best trial's ln Q compared with ln λ₁ from the same Gram (`constrained_prolate.py`; exact Gauss–Legendre nodes in ball arithmetic — numpy's double-precision nodes cap a band Gram at 10⁻¹⁶, fatal for 1 − λ ~ e^{−2c}; and mpmath's `qr` returns the full square Q, which the first draft used whole, making P = 0 — both caught by the trial's own diagnostics, −ln L = 0 and Q = O(1)).

**The result: the family is the ground state.** Even sector; ln λ₁ from the same basis; κ ≡ −ln L/(aT_c) is the constrained leakage exponent as a fraction of the concentration parameter c = aT_c (an unconstrained prolate has κ = 2 − O(ln c/c)):

The runs at δ = 2.0 and 2.3 also give the basis-size check of the previous addendum's values: −67.323 at m = 102 against −67.334 at m = 169.) Three structural facts, all read off the scans: (i) **the optimum dodges exactly the in-band zeros and no others** — θ_d = θ_c at every δ (at δ = 1.38, K = 8 is the count of zeros below 1.8T₀ = 45.1, and the band edge is 47.6; a zero just outside the band costs as much leakage to dodge as it removes from Q, a zero well outside costs nothing and removes nothing); (ii) **the band is 1.7–2.0 horizons wide**, not 0.8: A438's θ ≈ 0.8 was the product R/2π read as if the leakage exponent were the full Slepian 2c — it is κc with κ ≈ 0.73–1.0 and θ_c ≈ 2, the same product; (iii) **the residual factor ln Q − ln L ≈ 0.75–1.2** is the log of the zero density weighting the leaked mass, ln ln(T′/2π) with T′ ≈ 2.5–3T₀, exactly where A438 (iii) found half of Q to sit.

**The constant, located.** Since Q_best = λ₁·e^{gap} with gap ≤ 0.4, ln λ₁ = −κ(δ)·aT_c*(δ) + (ln Q − ln L) − gap, i.e.

R(δ) = π·κ(δ)·θ_c*(δ) − [(ln Q − ln L) + gap]/(δeᵟ) + o(1),

with the second term 0.33, 0.25, 0.10, 0.07 at δ = 1, 1.38, 2, 2.3: π·0.997·1.7 − 0.33 = 4.99 against the measured 5.11 at δ = 1; π·0.871·1.9 − 0.25 = 4.95 against 5.04 at δ = 1.38; π·0.815·1.8 − 0.10 = 4.51 against 4.56 at δ = 2; π·0.724·1.9 − 0.07 = 4.25 against 4.29 at δ = 2.3; π·0.589·2.0 − 0.03 = 3.67 against 3.68 at δ = 3 — the residual mismatch is the grid step (0.1 in θ_c is 0.3 in R) and the gap. **So R ≈ 5 is π × (a band of 1.7–1.9 horizons) × (a leakage ratio near 1), and it falls because κθ_c* falls — 1.69, 1.65, 1.47, 1.38, 1.18 at δ = 1, 1.38, 2, 2.3, 3 — the leakage ratio κ dropping (1.00, 0.87, 0.82, 0.72, 0.59) while the band radius stays at 1.7–2.0 horizons.** Neither κ(δ) nor θ_c*(δ) is derived here; they are the optimum of an explicit finite-dimensional problem, computed, and that is what "the constant" is at finite δ.

The slope Δf/Δδ falls linearly across δ = 2–3.5 (2.48, 1.99, 1.49, 1.04 at midpoints 2.15, 2.45, 2.8, 3.25 — a straight line that reaches zero at δ ≈ 4.0) and the last two intervals' slopes are 0.38 (3.5 → 3.75) and 0.06 (3.75 → 4): f is not approaching a constant along a 1/δ curve, it flattens faster — the δ = 3.75 point, computed after the δ = 4 surprise, sits below even the straight-line extrapolation of the slopes (0.55) and confirms that the δ = 4 value is not an artefact. *(Net state after A442: the flattening at δ = 3.75–4 is flagged there as a possible truncation effect of the 2000-zero list — the finite-δ balayage formula's offset jumps from its smooth O(δ) trend exactly at these two points — and should not be read as the law's asymptotic behaviour; A441 gives that.)* **What survives is the scaling statement: the δeᵟ form of A438 was the finite-range reading, and the exponent grows no faster than the horizon — −ln λ₁/T₀ is 1.45, 1.57, 1.66, 1.76, 1.84, 1.86 at δ = 2, 2.3, 2.6, 3, 3.5, 4 (1.857 at 3.75), a sequence whose increments are shrinking toward zero; whether it settles at a constant near 1.9 or turns over is not decided by the range reached here.** In the family's language κθ_c* = R/π falls 1.69 → 1.18 across δ = 1–3 with the band radius pinned at 1.7–2.0 horizons: the fill μ = 1 − (1 − ln θ_c)/δ of the band by the in-band zeros approaches 1, the constrained leakage ratio κ collapses (1.00, 0.87, 0.82, 0.72, 0.59), and the exponent −ln λ₁ = κ·aT_c* ≈ κθ_c*·πδeᵟ can only keep pace with T₀ if κθ_c* ∝ 1/δ — which is what the table says it is doing, to within the resolution of the last two points.

**What is derived, and the bound that fails to reach the constant.** Two classical pieces are now exact. (a) *The worst-case constraint model* of A438 (iv) — K constraints leave, by Courant–Fischer, a concentration of at least λ_K(c), so ln λ₁ ≤ −c·r(μ) + O(ln) with μ = K/(2c/π) — has its rate function in closed WKB form: with the turning point x_t fixed by the quantisation (2c/π)∫₀^{x_t}√((x_t² − x²)/(1 − x²))dx = k + ½, −ln(1 − λ_k) = 2c∫_{x_t}^1 √((x² − x_t²)/(1 − x²))dx + O(1); `prolate_wkb.py` checks it against the verified prolates of Theorem 1bl's machinery: at c = 100 the difference is +0.004 to +0.008 on exponents from 46 to 106, at c = 50 within 0.02 on exponents to 96, degrading only at the Shannon edge x_t → 1 (0.65 at k = 63 of 63.7). The fill at the optimum is μ = N(T_c)/(aT_c/π) = 1 − (1 − ln θ_c)/δ → 1, where the WKB rate vanishes like (1 − μ)/ln(1/(1 − μ)) (the tunnelling integral is (π/2)(1 − x_t) while 1 − μ ≈ ½(1 − x_t)ln(1/(1 − x_t)); numerically r/[(1 − μ)/ln(1/(1 − μ))] = 3.1, 3.7, 4.1 at 1 − μ = 10⁻², 10⁻³, 10⁻⁴, creeping toward 2π), so this bound's exponent is O(eᵟ/ln δ): it gives the eᵟ scaling up to a logarithm, the direction of the fall, and nothing about A. The actual zero constraints are far cheaper than the worst case (κ = 0.73 at δ = 2 against r(0.85) = 0.13), because the in-band zeros below T₀ are sub-Nyquist. (b) *The type-reduction construction* — factor out the in-band zeros as a sine-like product, losing type π × (local density), and take the prolate of the remaining type ½ln(T₀/t) — gives exponent ∫₀^{T}ln(T₀/t)dt = T(1 + ln(T₀/T)), maximal at T = T₀ with value T₀ = 2πeᵟ: the eᵟ scaling, with f ≥ 2π = 6.28. It is the right scaling and a factor ≈ 1.86 short (f flattens at 11.7 against 2π = 6.28), and it is short for an identifiable reason: dividing an entire function by a *polynomial* does not reduce its type — the factorisation ĝ = B_T·ĥ with B_T(r) = Π_{γ<T}(1 − r²/γ²) leaves ĥ in PW_a, and the constraint acts as the weight |B_T|², not as type loss; type loss is the infinite-sequence limit and undershoots at every finite T.

**One more derived piece: the weight is explicit and edge-loaded.** The size of the dodging product on the line is governed by the density *variation*, not the density: for a smooth zero count N(t) with density n(t), ln|B(r)| ≈ ∫ln|1 − r²/t²| n(t)dt, and the constant part of n contributes nothing (∫₀^∞ ln|1 − r²/t²|dt = 2r ln 2 − 2r ln 2 = 0 — the sine's envelope is flat). With n(t) = (1/2π)ln(t/2π) the varying part gives, for the product over *all* zeros, ln|B_∞(r)| ≈ (r/2π)∫₀^∞ ln|1 − u⁻²| ln u du = (r/2π)(−π²/2) = −πr/4 — the Γ-factor decay of Ξ(½ + ir) recovered from the zero density alone (the integral evaluates to −4.934802200 = −π²/2 to ten digits), which checks the calculus. For the *truncated* product B_T the missing factors leave an in-band growth ln|B_T(r)|² ≈ (δ/π)r²/T + O(T₀) (the omitted Π_{γ>T}(1 − r²/γ²) ≈ exp(−r²Σ_{γ>T}γ⁻²) would have damped it), so the weight |B_T|² rises toward the band edge like a Gaussian and, beyond it, like (r/T)^{4N(T)} — a log-slope (2/π)(δ + ln θ − 1) ≈ 4a/π at the edge, comparable to the probe's own type. That is why the ground state's mass and its residual both sit at and beyond the edge (A438 (iii); ln Q − ln L above), and it is the quantity the asymptotic analysis has to integrate against.

**Why the band extends past the horizon, and why type reduction stops there.** Zeros are a *global* budget for a function of exponential type a, not a local one: the Levinson–Cartwright density a/π per half-line is asymptotic, and a polynomial factor of any degree keeps the type at a, so nothing forbids a probe from vanishing on a stretch where the zeros are denser than a/π — it pays in concentration, not in admissibility. The natural accounting is the net spare count: below T₀ the zeros run a deficit against a/π that cumulates to eᵟ at the horizon, above it an excess eᵟ(x ln x − x + 1), net eᵟ·x(1 − ln x), which is spent by x = e. The ground state uses 0.4eᵟ of the deficit on the super-Nyquist stretch [T₀, 2T₀] (this is accounting, not a theorem: the optimum at 1.7–2.0 horizons is measured, and the vanishing of the net count at e horizons is where the accounting says the band must stop). Type reduction cannot follow it there: it assigns the zeros a *local* type πn(r) = ½ln(r/2π), which exceeds a beyond T₀, so the construction cannot extend past the horizon at all and its exponent is the band [−T₀, T₀]'s, T₀. The polynomial factorisation ĝ = B_T·ĥ is the admissible form on the whole band; what the borrowed stretch buys per zero is the content of κ, and that is the part not derived.

**The remaining problem, stated exactly (replacing A438's "frame constant").** Because the optimum dodges precisely the in-band zeros, λ₁ = min_T min_{ĥ ∈ PW_a} Σ_{γ>T}|B_T(γ)|²|ĥ(γ)|² / ∫|B_T ĥ|² up to the O(1) residual factor: a Slepian concentration problem with the polynomial weight |B_T|², degree 2N(T). Its large-δ asymptotics — the WKB/Landau–Widom analysis of (a) carried out with the weight — is the derivation of the constant; it is not done here *(net state: done in A440 — the exponent reduces to a scale-free equilibrium problem over the probe's zero distribution, solved to f_∞ = 12.56 ± 0.01 at a band of 2.00 horizons, i.e. −ln λ₁ → 2T₀; 4π conjectured)*, and the numbers above are the target it must hit (−ln λ₁/T₀ = 1.86 at δ = 4 and flattening; κθ_c* = 1.69, 1.65, 1.47, 1.38, 1.18 at δ = 1, 1.38, 2, 2.3, 3). No frame constant of the zero sequence is needed: the weight is explicit. Under RH nothing changes at finite δ (every value above is exact for the verified zeros); **nothing here bears on RH**. Checks 7/8 clean: the explicit formula, Slepian's problem, Courant–Fischer, WKB on the prolate equation — classical; no hypothesis input; no cascade quantity derived; the even sector only (the odd sector's constant is not treated).

**Instruments and corrections.** `constrained_prolate.py` (the family; grids and output by environment), `slack_law_flint.py` (the zero side with flint's eigensolver and the Rayleigh-ball check; `EXTRA` modes), `prolate_wkb.py` (the rate function against the verified prolates), `checkpoints/zeta_zeros_2000_hp.json` (the zero list at 36 digits — the double-precision list reproduces λ₁ at δ = 2 to eight digits, so it is adequate at every δ used here) — research instruments, cited by no paper surface, keyed by nothing; no hostile round is owed. A438 corrected in place: the δ = 3.0 even entry (1.763×10⁻⁹⁵ → 4.075×10⁻⁹⁷), the basis-size caveat on every entry (2–20% high in λ₁, ≤ 0.2 in ln λ₁), the "0.8T₀" reading of the mechanism (superseded by (ii) above), and the law's form (net-state marker on the δeᵟ sentence).

## Addendum 440 — the Landau–Widom analysis carried out (owner: "Carry out WKB or Landau–Widom analysis"): the slack law's exponent reduces, by Hadamard's product and the logarithmic potential of the probe's zero-count deviation, to a scale-free equilibrium problem in horizon units whose solution is f_∞ = lim −ln λ₁/eᵟ = 12.56 ± 0.01 at a band of exactly 2.00 ± 0.02 horizons — i.e. **−ln λ₁ → 2T₀ = 4πeᵟ** to the precision of the discretisation (4π = 12.566); the simplest admissible probe gives 11.76 at 2.35 horizons in closed integral form; the exact data approach from below (11.68 at δ = 4) with corrections that are O(log)-type per zero and quantified at δ = 2.3 by explicit probes; whether the constant is exactly 4π is open *(closed in A441: it is, by balayage)*

**Step 1 — the exponent is a potential.** Take the probe ĝ real, even, of exponential type a = δ/2, with real zeros (the prolate's class; the dodging prolate of A439 is built from such). Hadamard's product gives, exactly, ln|ĝ(r)| = ln|ĝ(0)| + Σ_k ln|1 − r²/z_k²| over the probe's zeros z_k > 0, i.e. ln|ĝ(r)| = const + ∫ ln|1 − r²/t²| dM(t) with M the probe's zero count on (0, t). A uniform density contributes a flat envelope — ∫₀^∞ ln|1 − r²/t²| dt = 2r ln 2 − 2r ln 2 = 0, which is why sin(ar) is bounded — so with D(t) = M(t) − (a/π)t the log-envelope is u(r) = ∫ ln|1 − r²/t²| dD(t) up to O(log r) (the discrete-versus-smooth error, the sine's −ln(ar), the norm's width). The probe must contain the zeta zeros on its dodging band [0, T]: dM ≥ dN there; beyond T its zeros are its own; Cartwright's class fixes the asymptotic density a/π, i.e. D(t) = o(t), and L² needs a net deficit of at least half a zero. Then, at exponential accuracy, ‖g‖² ≍ e^{2 max u} and Q(g) = Σ_γ|ĝ(γ)|² ≍ e^{2 sup_{γ>T} u}, so ln λ₁ = 2[sup_{r>T} u − max_r u] + O(log).

**Step 2 — the problem is scale-free in horizon units.** Put r = T₀x, t = T₀y, D = eᵟρ. The kernel is invariant, ln|1 − r²/t²| = ln|1 − x²/y²|, and the zeta deviation is δ-independent: N(T₀y) = eᵟy(δ + ln y − 1) against the Nyquist count eᵟδy gives dρ_N = ln y dy — a deficit below the horizon (total 1 at y = 1: the eᵟ spare degrees of freedom of A439) and an excess above it. Hence u = eᵟφ with φ(x) = ∫ ln|1 − x²/y²| dρ(y), and

f_∞ = lim −ln λ₁/eᵟ = 2 · max over X and ρ of [ max_{x ≤ X} φ(x) − sup_{x > X} φ(x) ],  dρ ≥ ln y dy on [0, X], ρ free beyond X, ρ(∞) ≤ 0.

This is the derivation of the eᵟ scaling: the constraint pins the deficit to O(eᵟ) (a probe free of zeros in its band, the prolate, may run a deficit of order δeᵟ and pays back with the Slepian exponent 2c = πδXeᵟ; the zeta zeros forbid that). Substituting v = x², w = y² turns ln|1 − x²/y²| into ln|v − w| − ln w: a logarithmic potential on the half-line, and the problem is a weighted equilibrium problem of classical potential theory — choose the probe's compensating zeros beyond the band to minimise the potential's supremum there, in the external field of the zeta deviation.

**Step 3 — the simplest probe, in closed integral form.** Zeta zeros on [0, X], Nyquist density beyond: φ(x) = ∫₀^X ln|1 − x²/y²| ln y dy. Its in-band maximum is at x = 0 (φ(0) = 0) and its supremum beyond X sits at x ≈ 1.4X; f(X) = −2 sup_{x>X} φ rises to **11.756 at X = 2.35** (11.35 at 2.0, 11.67 at 2.2, 11.75 at 2.4, 11.47 at 2.6) — a rigorous lower bound within the model, already at the level of the measured f(4) = 11.68 and with the residual landing at 3.3 horizons (A438 (iii) measured 2.5 at finite δ). For X > e the far field grows (X ln X − X > 0): the accounting limit of A439 appears here as the condition for the envelope to decay.

**Step 4 — the equilibrium problem, solved numerically.** Discretising ρ on cells with the cell-integrated kernel (∫ ln|1 − x²/y²| dy = [G(y − x) + G(y + x) − 2G(y)], G(z) = z ln|z| − z, exact per cell) and imposing φ(x_j) ≤ s on a dense set beyond X, φ(x_i) ≤ φ(0) inside, dρ ≥ ln y dy inside, ρ(∞) ≤ 0, the problem is a linear programme (`lw_continuum.py`). Its value rises with refinement — 12.544 (400 + 800 cells), 12.555 (800 + 1600), 12.558 (1200 + 2400, Y = 200 horizons) — toward **f_∞ = 12.56 ± 0.01**, with the optimum at **X* = 2.00 ± 0.02** at every refinement (12.5434 / 12.5441 / 12.5431 and 12.5547 / 12.5553 / 12.5545 at X = 1.98 / 2.00 / 2.02 on the two coarser grids; the finest grid reached X = 1.98 before the process was killed for memory alongside the δ = 4.25 run). The optimal probe: zeta zeros on the band of two horizons, no extra zeros inside, and beyond the edge an excess of its own zeros of total mass 2(1 − ln 2) = 0.614eᵟ — exactly the in-band deficit, so the net count is zero (the constraint is active) — placed to hold φ at the constant s over the stretch just beyond the edge (the equilibrium condition; density ≈ 1.1–1.3 × Nyquist just past the edge, decaying). Extra zeros inside the band never help; deficits beyond the band never help. So

**−ln λ₁ = f_∞·eᵟ + O(δ) with f_∞ = 12.56 ± 0.01 = (2.00 ± 0.002)·2π: the slack law's exponent is twice the horizon, ln λ₁ ≈ −2T₀ = −4πeᵟ, on a band of two horizons.** Whether f_∞ is exactly 4π (12.5664) is not decided by the discretisation (0.006 below it on the finest grid, still rising); it is stated as a conjecture, with the equilibrium problem above as the object whose exact solution would settle it.

**Step 5 — against the exact data, and the finite-δ corrections.** The exact zero side gives f = 9.11, 9.86, 10.46, 11.05, 11.57, 11.67, 11.68 at δ = 2, 2.3, 2.6, 3, 3.5, 3.75, 4 (A439), approaching 12.56 from below. The gap is finite-δ structure that the continuum drops: (i) the smooth zero count is negative below y = e^{1−δ} (the first zero sits at 0.22, 0.11, 0.04 horizons at δ = 2.3, 3, 4) so the in-band deviation is not ln y there; (ii) the probe's own zeros are eᵟδ per horizon, a "continuum" of only ~30 per horizon at δ = 2.3; (iii) the O(log) terms — the sine factor, the norm's width, and the number of zeta zeros over which the residual is summed when φ is held flat (the LP flattens it over tens of horizons: a ln N ≈ 7-nat cost it does not see). Re-running the LP with the zeta zeros discrete (`lw_semidiscrete.py`) predicts f = 10.43, 11.39, 12.07 at δ = 2.3, 3, 4 (against 9.86, 11.05, 11.68): the discreteness of the zeta zeros accounts for about a third of the gap and the O(log) terms for the rest. The rest was measured directly: building the semi-discrete optimum as an explicit probe at δ = 2.3 (`probe_test.py`: 41 zeta zeros, 875 designed zeros to 40 horizons, a Nyquist grid beyond, evaluated at 120 digits) gives an exact Rayleigh quotient of e^{−89.2} against the model's e^{−104.0} — 15 nats of O(log) slack — while the simplest probe built the same way gives e^{−91.6}, within 6.7 nats of λ₁ = e^{−98.3}. Two conclusions: the ground state's structure (zeta zeros on the band, near-Nyquist zeros beyond) is confirmed by explicit construction to within seven nats at δ = 2.3, and the model's optimum is reached only asymptotically, where the O(log) terms are O(δ) against eᵟ.

**What is now derived, and what remains.** Derived: the eᵟ scaling (Step 2), the reduction to a classical equilibrium problem (Steps 1–2), a closed-form lower bound 11.76 (Step 3), and the constant to three digits, f_∞ = 12.56, X* = 2.00 (Step 4). A438's δeᵟ form and A439's "flattening" are both finite-δ readings of this single law. Open: ~~the exact value (4π conjectured)~~ *(A441 proves f_∞ = 4π within the reduced problem)*, and a controlled expansion of the finite-δ corrections. Checks 7/8 clean: Hadamard, Cartwright, logarithmic potential theory, linear programming — classical; no hypothesis input; no cascade quantity derived; even sector only. **Nothing here bears on RH** (every quantity is a property of the first two thousand verified zeros and their smooth count).

**Instruments.** `tools/research/slack_law/` (README there): `lw_variational.py`, `lw_lp.py`, `lw_continuum.py`, `lw_semidiscrete.py`, `probe_test.py`, `probe_profile.py`, the LP solutions as JSON — research instruments, cited by no paper surface, keyed by nothing; no hostile round is owed.

## Addendum 441 — f_∞ = 4π proved within the reduced problem (owner: "Prove 4 pi"): the equilibrium problem of A440 is solved in closed form by balayage onto the doubly slit plane — f(X) = 2πX(1 + ln 2 − ln X), maximal at exactly X* = 2 with f_∞ = 4π, the optimal potential exactly −2π on the whole exterior; the ingredients are the Green function of ℂ ∖ ((−∞, −X] ∪ [X, ∞)) with pole at 0, one integral evaluated by parts, and the maximum principle for optimality; the balayage is admissible (a genuine zero excess) for X ≤ 2.05, so the maximiser is admissible; A440's conjecture is closed, and the theorem is conditional only on A440's Step 1 (the reduction)

**The problem, as a logarithmic potential.** A440 Step 2: f_∞ = 2·max over X and ρ of [max_{x≤X} φ − sup_{x>X} φ] with φ(x) = ∫₀^∞ ln|1 − x²/y²| dρ(y), dρ ≥ ln y dy on [0, X] (the zeta deviation from Nyquist, in horizon units), ρ free beyond X, ρ(∞) ≤ 0. Write σ for the even extension of ρ to ℝ and U^σ(x) = ∫ ln|x − y| dσ(y) for its logarithmic potential; since ln|1 − x²/y²| = ln|x − y| + ln|x + y| − 2 ln|y|, φ(x) = U^σ(x) − U^σ(0) exactly. In particular φ(0) = 0 for every ρ, so once φ ≤ 0 on the band (checked below for the optimum) the in-band maximum is 0 and

f(X) = −2·min over admissible σ of sup_{E} [U^σ − U^σ(0)],  E = {|x| ≥ X}.

Split σ = σ₀ + τ with σ₀ = ln|y| dy on [−X, X] (fixed: a deficit on |y| < 1, an excess on 1 < |y| < X, total mass σ₀(ℝ) = 2(X ln X − X) < 0 for X < e) and τ the probe's own zeros — a positive measure on E (extra zeros inside the band are also allowed; deficits on E are allowed in the LP and are handled by the optimality argument), of total mass at most −σ₀(ℝ) = 2X(1 − ln X).

**The solution: balayage.** Let Ω = ℂ ∖ E, the plane slit along the two rays, and let τ be the balayage of −σ₀ onto E = ∂Ω — the signed measure on E whose potential agrees with that of −σ₀ on E. Because ∞ is a boundary point of Ω the balayage preserves both the potential on E and the total mass, so U^{σ₀+τ} ≡ 0 on E, the net count σ(ℝ) is exactly 0 (the mass constraint is active, as the LP found), and

φ|_E ≡ s := −U^{σ₀+τ}(0) = −∫ ln|t| dσ₀(t) − ∫_E ln|x| dτ(x) = ∫ [h(t) − ln|t|] dσ₀(t) = ∫_{−X}^{X} g_Ω(t, 0) ln|t| dt,

where h is the harmonic extension of ln|x| from E into Ω and g_Ω(·, 0) = h − ln|·| is the Green function of Ω with pole at 0 (harmonic off 0, zero on E, +∞ at 0). The potential is *constant* on the entire exterior: the equilibrium condition of A440's LP ("φ held at s beyond the edge") holds on all of E.

**The Green function and the two integrals.** The map w = ζ/(1 + √(1 − ζ²)), ζ = z/X, sends Ω onto the unit disc with 0 ↦ 0 (its inverse is ζ = 2w/(1 + w²)), so g_Ω(t, 0) = −ln|w(t/X)| = ln[(1 + √(1 − t²/X²))·X/t] for 0 < t < X. With t = Xu:

s(X) = 2X ∫₀¹ ln((1 + √(1 − u²))/u)·(ln X + ln u) du = 2X (A ln X + B),

A = ∫₀¹ ln((1 + √(1 − u²))/u) du = ∫₀^{π/2} ln(1 + cos θ) cos θ dθ + 1 = (π/2 − 1) + 1 = π/2 (by parts: [sin θ ln(1 + cos θ)] + ∫ sin²θ/(1 + cos θ) = ∫₀^{π/2}(1 − cos θ) dθ),

B = ∫₀¹ ln((1 + √(1 − u²))/u) ln u du = B₁ − 2, B₁ = ∫₀^{π/2} ln(1 + cos θ) ln(sin θ) cos θ dθ = ∫₀^{π/2} (1 − cos θ)(ln sin θ − 1) dθ = −(π/2) ln 2 + 1 − (π/2 − 1) = 2 − (π/2)(1 + ln 2)

(by parts with ∫ ln(sin θ) cos θ dθ = sin θ ln sin θ − sin θ, the boundary terms vanishing at both ends, then ∫₀^{π/2} ln sin θ dθ = −(π/2) ln 2). Hence **B = −(π/2)(1 + ln 2)** (numerically −2.6595893719 both ways), s(X) = πX(ln X − 1 − ln 2), and

**f(X) = −2 s(X) = 2πX (1 + ln 2 − ln X),  f′(X) = 2π(ln 2 − ln X) = 0 ⇔ X* = 2,  f(2) = 4π.**

**Optimality (the maximum principle).** Let τ′ be any admissible competitor (positive extra mass inside the band, any signed density on E, total mass ≤ −σ₀(ℝ)) and ν = τ′ − τ. Then U^ν − U^ν(0) is subharmonic in Ω (harmonic if τ′ has no mass inside), vanishes at the origin, and φ′ − φ = U^ν − U^ν(0). Suppose sup_E φ′ < s. Then U^ν − U^ν(0) < 0 on E. At infinity: if ν(ℝ) < 0, U^ν → −∞; if ν(ℝ) = 0, U^ν → 0 so U^ν − U^ν(0) → −U^ν(0). If U^ν(0) > 0 every boundary value of the subharmonic function is negative, so it is negative throughout Ω — contradicting its value 0 at the origin. If U^ν(0) ≤ 0 and ν is neutral, then φ′ − φ → −U^ν(0) ≥ 0 along E toward infinity, so sup_E φ′ ≥ s — contradiction again. Hence s(X) is the minimum over *all* admissible competitors, signed or not: the closed form f(X) = 2πX(1 + ln 2 − ln X) is an upper bound on the equilibrium value for every X, attained exactly when the balayage itself is admissible, i.e. when the density of τ = −(σ₀)^ is non-negative on E.

**Admissibility.** The balayage of a point mass at t ∈ (−X, X) is the harmonic measure of Ω seen from t: in the disc picture the boundary point x = X/cos θ (both sides of the slit, θ and −θ) receives P(w(t/X), θ) dθ/π with P the Poisson kernel, and dx = X sin θ/cos²θ dθ. Integrating against −ln|t| dt (`balayage_check.py`): at X = 2 the density is positive on all of E — 0.672 per unit length at the edge, 0.069 at 2X, positive to the last node at 4000 — with one-sided mass 0.6134 against the required 2(1 − ln 2)/2 = 0.6137; the potential φ is −6.2859, −6.2826, −6.2845, −6.2834, −6.2828, −6.2830, −6.2835 at x/X = 1.001, 1.05, 1.3, 2, 4, 10, 100 (−2π = −6.2832); inside the band φ = −0.05, −0.96, −2.27, −3.44, −4.13, −5.03, −5.75, −6.22, −6.28 at x = 0.01, 0.2, 0.5, 0.8, 1, 1.3, 1.6, 1.9, 2 — monotone from 0 at the origin to −2π at the edge, so the in-band maximum is at 0 and the norm reading of A440 Step 1 stands. The edge density falls through zero between X = 2.0 (+0.75) and X = 2.1 (−0.73): for X ≳ 2.05 the unconstrained balayage wants to *remove* zeros at the edge, the true value lies strictly below the closed form there, and the closed form's maximiser X = 2 sits inside the admissible range. Therefore

**f_∞ = max_X f(X) = 4π exactly, at X* = 2: −ln λ₁ = 4πeᵟ(1 + o(1)) = 2T₀(1 + o(1)), on a dodging band of exactly two horizons, with the residual held at the uniform exponential level e^{−2π·2eᵟ} over the entire zero region beyond the band — conditional on A440's Step 1.**

This closes A440's conjecture: the LP values 12.544 / 12.555 / 12.558 approached 4π = 12.5664 from below as their grids refined, with X* = 2.00 ± 0.02 throughout; the LP's edge density 0.62 is the balayage's 0.67 seen through a cell; its zero net count is the mass conservation of balayage.

**Remarks.** (i) Only the density of the zeros entered: the same argument for a degree-d density (d/2π)ln(t/2π) scales σ₀ by d and the horizon to T₀(d) = 2πe^{δ/d}, giving −ln λ₁ → 4πd·e^{δ/d} = 2d·T₀(d) (with the admissibility threshold to be rechecked). (ii) The two exact numbers, X* = 2 and s = −2π, come from A = π/2 and B = −(π/2)(1 + ln 2), i.e. from the Green function of the doubly slit plane against ln t: the "twice the horizon" and "4π per spare degree of freedom" of A440 are the Joukowski map and ∫₀^{π/2} ln sin θ dθ = −(π/2) ln 2. (iii) What remains for an unconditional theorem is A440's Step 1 — that the exponent of the true λ₁ equals the value of the equilibrium problem: the upper bound λ₁ ≤ exp(−(4π − ε)eᵟ) by explicit construction of the balayage probe with Euler–Maclaurin control of the discrete-versus-smooth error, and the lower bound, which needs the extremality of real-zero probes. Neither is done here. Checks 7/8 clean: Hadamard, balayage, the Green function of a slit plane, the maximum principle — classical; no hypothesis input; no cascade quantity derived. **Nothing here bears on RH.**

**Instruments.** `tools/research/slack_law/balayage_check.py` (research instrument, cited by no paper surface, keyed by nothing; no hostile round is owed): B by quadrature, the balayage density by the disc Poisson kernel, the potential on E and inside, the closed-form f(X), and the admissibility threshold.

## Addendum 442 — the remaining piece attacked (owner: "Attack the remaining piece"): the reduction of the true λ₁ to the equilibrium problem is broken into five lemmas, each classical in kind and each checked numerically on the exact ground states; the balayage argument carried out with the actual discrete zeros gives an explicit finite-δ formula, ln λ₁ = min_T [4 Σ_{γ<T} ln((1 + √(1 − γ²/T²))·T/γ) − 2aT] + c(δ), that tracks the exact values with c(δ) = 4.7, 5.2, 5.9, 6.4, 6.6, 7.2, 7.9 nats at δ = 1 … 3.5 — an O(δ) correction against exponents of 14 … 383 — and whose continuum limit is −4πeᵟ; the lower bound needs no real-zero assumption (the maximum principle absorbs complex zeros); what is left for an unconditional theorem is the rigorous form of the five lemmas, not any new idea; an anomaly in the offset at δ = 3.75–4 is flagged as a possible convergence problem of the "exact" values there

**The finite-δ formula.** Run A441's balayage with the zeta zeros left discrete. The fixed part of the zero-deviation measure is σ₀ = Σ_{0<γ<T}(δ_γ + δ_{−γ}) − (a/π)dt on [−T, T]; its balayage onto E = {|x| ≥ T} makes the exterior potential constant at s_δ(T) = ∫ g_Ω(t, 0) dσ₀(t) = 2Σ_{γ<T} g_T(γ) − aT, with g_T(t) = ln[(1 + √(1 − t²/T²))·T/t] the Green function of the doubly slit plane and (a/π)·2∫₀^T g_T = (a/π)·T·(π/2)·2 = aT. The model's prediction is therefore

ln λ₁ ≈ min over T of 2 s_δ(T) = min_T [ 4 Σ_{γ<T} ln((1 + √(1 − γ²/T²))·T/γ) − 2aT ] + O(log),

with dg_T/dT = 1/√(T² − t²) giving d(2s_δ)/dT ≈ ln(T/2T₀) + O(1/δ): the minimum sits at T ≈ 2T₀ for every δ, and Euler–Maclaurin on the zero sum (N(t) = smooth count + O(ln t)) gives 2s_δ(2T₀) = −4πeᵟ + O(δ) — measured: 2s_δ(2T₀) + 4πeᵟ = 16.8, 17.9, 19.9, 21.2, 21.9, 23.5, 25.3, 26.9 at δ = 1, 1.5, 2, 2.3, 2.6, 3, 3.5, 4 (`discrete_balayage.py`). Against the exact zero side:

| δ | T*/T₀ | min_T 2s_δ | exact ln λ₁ | c(δ) = exact − formula | c/δ |

| 1.0 | 1.78 | −18.570 | −13.883 | 4.69 | 4.7 |
| 1.3828 | 1.92 | −32.959 | −27.759 | 5.20 | 3.8 |

The formula reproduces the semi-discrete LP of A440 (−104.0, −228.8, −659.0 at δ = 2.3, 3, 4): that LP *was* the discrete balayage. Through δ = 3.5 the offset c(δ) grows like 2.2 + 1.6δ — the O(log) terms of A440 Step 1 (the norm's width, the sine factor, the number of zeta zeros summed at the flat level, ln 2π), each O(δ) — against exponents that grow like eᵟ: the model captures the exponent to 2% at δ = 3.5. **Flag:** at δ = 3.75 and 4 the offset jumps to 12.3 and 21.4, breaking the smooth trend. The exact values there are the ones that made f flatten in A439; the jump is evidence that they are under-converged — most likely the zero list (2000 zeros, ending at 7.3T₀ at δ = 4 against 20T₀ at δ = 3) with the density tail beyond it, since the flat exterior potential makes the residual sum over every listed zero. This is not resolved here; it does not touch the analytic result (which is a δ → ∞ statement) but it reopens the "flattening" reading of A439, which should be re-read as a truncation effect until a longer zero list settles it. *(Net state, the recheck commissioned by the owner: the zero list is NOT the cause — 700 against 2000 zeros at δ = 3.5 moves ln λ₁ by 0.03 nats, 1000 against 2000 at δ = 3.75 by 0.06, and the extended 6700-zero list (to height 6997, 26 horizons at δ = 3.75) reproduces the 2000-zero value at δ = 3.75 to 0.001 nats (−496.129 against −496.128); the cause is the Legendre basis: at δ = 3.75, 300 extra modes give ln λ₁ = −500.529 against −496.128 at 120, and with it the offset falls back to 7.9 nats, exactly on the smooth trend. The δ = 3.75 and δ = 4 values of A439's table are under-converged in the basis by 4.4 and (the δ = 4 large-basis run in flight) more; the "flattening" was a basis artefact. Recorded in the Theorem 1bm landing, A443.)*

**The lower bound needs no real-zero assumption.** A440 stated the reduction for real-zero probes. The optimality argument of A441 does not need it: for any competitor with zero measure σ′ in ℂ (Hadamard's product for the Cartwright class is exact for complex zeros too, with ln|F(x)| − ln|F(x₀)| = U^{D_F}(x) − U^{D_F}(x₀)), the difference potential is subharmonic in Ω = ℂ ∖ E, and the maximum principle applies verbatim. So the extremal is real-zero *because* the balayage is, not by assumption.

**The five lemmas.** With that, the equivalence "ln λ₁ = 2 s_δ(T*) + O(δ)" — and hence f_∞ = 4π unconditionally — reduces to:

1. *Near-vanishing is vanishing.* A probe of type a with |F(γ)| ≤ e^{−M} at a zeta zero γ where its envelope exceeds e^{−M} has a zero within e^{−M}·O(a) of γ (Bernstein), and moving a zero by that distance changes the potential by o(1) uniformly away from it; a probe that instead lowers its envelope to e^{−M} at γ by clustering zeros is bounded by Jensen's local zero-count estimate n(x₀, R) ≤ eaR + O(1), which caps the cluster at O(1) zeros per Nyquist spacing — far below what a dip of depth ~eᵟ needs. So at exponential accuracy every competitor contains the zeta zeros on the part of the band where its envelope is above the residual level, which is the constraint dρ ≥ dρ_N on [0, X] with X chosen by the competitor.
2. *The pole sits at the origin.* For a competitor whose norm peaks at x₀ ≠ 0, the same balayage with pole x₀ gives s(x₀) = ∫ g_Ω(t, x₀) dσ₀(t) ≥ s(0): checked, s(x₀) = −6.28, −5.80, −4.87, −3.61, −2.15, −0.75, −0.07 at x₀ = 0, 0.1, 0.3, 0.6, 1.0, 1.5, 1.9 (X = 2). A proof should follow from the monotonicity of the Green function's Poisson representation in the pole; not written.
3. *Sampling on the exterior.* The residual is Σ_{γ∈E}|F(γ)|², the model's is the envelope's supremum on E; the two agree at exponential accuracy iff sup_E|F| ≤ e^{o(eᵟ)}·max_{γ∈E}|F(γ)|. The zeta zeros on E are super-Nyquist by the factor 1 + ln x/δ, so this is a Landau–Beurling sampling inequality with a constant that may grow like e^{O(δ)} but not like e^{ceᵟ}. Checked on the exact ground states: ln sup_E|ĝ| − ln max_{γ∈E}|ĝ(γ)| = 0.97, 0.84, 0.40 (δ = 1, E beyond 1.5, 2, 2.5 horizons) and 1.14, 0.94, 0.92 (δ = 1.38) — one nat.
4. *Euler–Maclaurin for the designed zeros.* In the construction (upper bound), the probe's own zeros are placed along the balayage density, which is smooth and bounded on E (0.67 at the edge, decaying); the discrete-versus-smooth error of their potential is O(log) per unit length of the log-singular kernel — the same estimate that made sin(ar) bounded.
5. *The discrete-to-continuum limit.* 2 s_δ(2T₀) = −4πeᵟ + O(δ), by Euler–Maclaurin on Σ_{γ<T} g_T(γ) with N(t) = (t/2π)ln(t/2πe) + O(ln t) (the boundary term at the first zero and the region where the smooth count is negative are O(δ)); measured above.

Lemmas 1–3 are the lower bound (for every F ∈ PW_a, sup over the non-dodged zeta zeros of |F(γ)|/|F(x₀)| is at least e^{s_δ(T) − O(δ)} for the competitor's own T, hence Q ≥ e^{2 min_T s_δ − O(δ)}‖F‖²), Lemma 4 is the upper bound (the balayage probe achieves 2s_δ + O(δ)), Lemma 5 converts both to 4π. None requires a new idea; each is a quantified version of a classical statement (Bernstein and Jensen; the Poisson kernel; Landau's sampling theorem; Euler–Maclaurin), and each has now been checked on the exact ground states. The honest status: the theorem f_∞ = 4π is proved conditional on these five, which are stated precisely enough to be attacked one at a time; the finite-δ formula with its O(δ) offset is the quantitative form the whole thing takes, and it holds on the data through δ = 3.5 to 2%.

Checks 7/8 clean: Hadamard, Bernstein, Jensen, Landau sampling, Euler–Maclaurin, the maximum principle — classical; no hypothesis input; no cascade quantity derived. **Nothing here bears on RH.** Instruments: `tools/research/slack_law/discrete_balayage.py` (research instrument, cited by no paper surface, keyed by nothing; no hostile round is owed).

## Addendum 447 — the prior art of the slack law found (owner: search for "an archimedean positivity source that dominates the prime side without consulting the zeros, or a prime-side inequality at unbounded support (which is RH restated), or an object with the arithmetic built in rather than the archimedean-local factors the paper itself proved are RH-blind"): the exponential-of-exponential decay of the same eigenvalue is in print twice before Theorem 1bm — Connes–Consani (ζ-cycles, 2023, sec. 2.5, numerically to µ ≈ 8) and Connes (arXiv 2602.04022, February 2026, sec. 6.4, to λ² = 17, matched by graph to the prolate law 1 − χ₂ ∼ (2¹⁴/3)√2π⁵ e^{−4πe^L + 9L/2} — the constant as corrected in place by round 293 F293-1) — so the constant 4π is in print as the prolate's; clause (vii) added to the block, gate g12 (the normalisation checked live at δ = log 2: 1.3292×10⁻³ against their "∼ 0.00133"; the residual ln λ₁ + 4πeᵟ pinned, slope 5.04 per unit δ), round 293 commissioned

**The search, as run.** Web searches on the three named items, then the primary texts: Connes–Consani, *Weil positivity and trace formula, the archimedean place* (arXiv 2006.13771, `CC2020.txt`), Connes–Consani, *Spectral triples and ζ-cycles* (arXiv 2106.01715, Enseign. Math. 69 (2023), `zetacycles.txt`, page renders `zc_p23.png`/`zc_p24.png`), Connes, *The Riemann Hypothesis: Past, Present and a Letter Through Time* (arXiv 2602.04022, February 5, 2026, `Connes2026_full.txt`, page renders `cn_p28.png`/`cn_p29.png`); Bombieri (Rend. Lincei 2000), Suzuki (arXiv 2301.00421), Xian-Jin Li (arXiv 2404.13427), Deninger (arXiv 2410.20758, 2508.15971) by abstract and prior record. Text extraction by pypdf; page renders by pymupdf (installed this session; the tool-results PDFs are in the session directory).

**The three items, answered.** *(a) An archimedean positivity source that dominates the prime side without consulting the zeros:* the only proven instance is Connes–Consani 2020, Theorem 1 — "Let g ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ*₊) have support in the interval [2^{-1/2}, 2^{1/2}] and Fourier transform vanishing at i/2 and 0. Then W_∞(g⋆g*) ≥ Tr(ϑ(g)Sϑ(g)*)" — the archimedean term dominating on support log 2 (Theorem 6.11 there with a constant 13 < c < 17), i.e. exactly the threshold the paper's 1bj–1bl passed with interval arithmetic; beyond log 2 no archimedean dominance is proved anywhere, and Connes' 2026 sec. 6.6 states what remains for his own route ("one needs to show that the smallest eigenvalue of the Weil quadratic form QW_λ is simple with even eigenvector … Moreover it still remains to show that k_λ is a sufficiently good approximation of θ_x"). *(b) A prime-side inequality at unbounded support:* Robin/Lagarias (σ(n)), Nyman–Beurling/Báez-Duarte (L² distance), Li's criterion (λ_n ≥ 0) — each an equivalence, RH restated, as the owner's phrasing anticipated; nothing in the record is a route through them. *(c) An object with the arithmetic built in:* Connes–Consani's scaling site / adelic prolate operator (2024) and the ζ-cycles spectral triple (its low-lying spectrum "mimics the low lying zeros" by construction through 2π/ζ_n — the zeros put in, not out); Deninger's foliated dynamical systems (a programme, no positivity theorem); Suzuki's de Branges construction (conditional on RH); Li's operator (unverified). None dominates the prime side without the zeros. **No route.**

**The finding that matters (Check 2 on the paper's own claims).** Both Connes–Consani papers and the 2026 survey compute the paper's object: the semi-local Weil form on [λ⁻¹, λ] (the bridge `oneprime_bridge.py`: their σ⁺ form IS the 1az operator term by term), L = 2 log λ = δ. Verbatim: ζ-cycles sec. 2.5, "Pushing the computations further and increasing the precision, one obtains an estimate of the size of the smallest eigenvalue s(L) of the even matrix, as a function of µ = exp L. One finds an exponential behavior, as reported in Figures 18 and 19, where log s(L) is plotted in terms of µ = exp L." — Figure 18 (rendered, read by the lead) is near-linear in µ, no constant stated (the lead's reading "roughly −85 at µ = 8" was wrong: round 293 F293-2 digitised the vector path — the curve runs to µ = 9.0, −74.2 at µ = 8, −86.0 at µ = 9, and −27.65 at µ = 3.986, −67.02 at µ = 7.389 against the cells' −27.765, −67.332); Figure 5's caption, "The smallest eigenvalue when L = log 2 is ∼ 0.00133".
